title: General Manager-Legal
description:
Role Overview The GM Legal will lead and manage all litigation and dispute resolution matters for the renewable energy business, including solar, wind, hybrid, storage, transmission, and related infrastructure. The role requires deep understanding of sector‑specific regulatory frameworks, commercial disputes, land‑related litigation, EPC and O&M issues, and government interface. --
Key Responsibilities1. Litigation Strategy & Management - Manage and oversee all litigation across civil, commercial, regulatory, arbitration, criminal, environmental, labour, and land acquisition matters. - Develop and implement litigation strategy aligned with business goals and project timelines. - Provide risk analysis and strategic inputs for high‑value disputes and contingencies. - Ensure effective case lifecycle management including tracking, reporting, and closure.
2. Renewable SectorSpecific Dispute Handling - Handle disputes related to: - EPC/O&M contractors - Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) - Open access, transmission, and grid‑connectivity issues - Land acquisition, ROW, and local authority challenges - DISCOMs and state nodal agencies - SLDC / RLDC / CERC / SERC regulatory litigation - Support negotiations for tariff issues, curtailment, scheduling, penalties, liquidated damages, and performance claims.
3. Regulatory & Government Interface - Draft and review replies for regulatory bodies: CERC, SERCs, MNRE, SECI, revenue authorities, forest/environment departments, and state land authorities. - Handle show‑cause notices, compliance matters, and appeals before tribunals. - Represent the organisation in government hearings, regulatory proceedings, and compliance audits.
4. External Counsel & Advisor Management - Identify, empanel, and manage external advocates and law firms across multiple states. - Review pleadings, statements, notices, and legal opinions prepared by counsel. - Ensure high‑quality representation and cost optimisation. ### 5. Contractual & Documentation Support - Review litigation‑sensitive clauses in EPC contracts, PPAs, land agreements, vendor contracts, and financing documents. - Ensure documentation, evidence, and internal approvals for litigation are timely and accurate. - Oversee drafting of replies, complaints, petitions, affidavits, and arbitration submissions.
6. Internal Advisory & Stakeholder Coordination - Collaborate closely with Projects, EPC, Finance, Land, Regulatory, and Operations teams. - Conduct internal investigations, fact‑finding exercises, and legal audits. - Provide preventive legal advisory to reduce disputes.
7. Governance, Risk & Compliance - Build SOPs for dispute resolution and legal risk mitigation. - Conduct training on litigation risk, regulatory compliance, and contract safeguards. - Monitor legal budgets, case outcomes, timelines, and recurring risk patterns. ---
Qualifications & Experience - LL.B / LL.M from a reputed law school. - 10-15+ years of experience in litigation, preferably in energy, infrastructure, EPC, or utilities. - Strong exposure to regulatory bodies like CERC, SERCs, APTEL, and state authorities. - Experience handling arbitration, high‑stake commercial disputes, and land‑related matters. - Prior leadership experience in managing multi‑state litigation portfolios.
Key Skills & Competencies - Deep knowledge of the Electricity Act, renewable energy regulations, transmission codes, land laws, and contract laws. - Strong analytical, drafting, and negotiation skills. - Ability to handle high‑pressure, time‑sensitive regulatory matters. - Excellent stakeholder and cross‑functional coordination abilities. - High integrity, strong business acumen, and leadership maturity.

title: Intelligence Officer
description:
Intelligence Officer

ROLE PROFILE

GENERAL

Date

April 2026

Location

Aggeneys, Northern Cape

Operations

BMC Shared Services

Job Grade

Paterson C4 / Vedanta M8

ROLE CONTEXT

The Intelligence Officer forms part of the HSE & ESG security function and provides operational intelligence support to protect people, assets, information and critical infrastructure.

• The role gathers, verifies, assesses and communicates security-related information from lawful internal and external sources.

• The role supports prevention and response relating to theft, fraud, illegal mining, organised crime, vandalism, unauthorised access, community-related security risks and threats to business continuity.

· The position works under the direction of the Security Coordinator and interfaces with Operations, HSE, ESG, Community Relations, HR, Legal, Supply Chain, IT and relevant law-enforcement agencies.

PURPOSE OF THE ROLE

To collect, evaluate, analyse and report security intelligence that enables proactive risk mitigation, informed decision-making and effective incident prevention across VZI/BMM operations.

• Produce timely intelligence assessments, alerts and actionable recommendations.

• Maintain lawful, ethical and confidential intelligence processes and records.

• Support investigations and security operations through evidence-based intelligence.

• Monitor emerging threats and patterns that may affect employees, operations, assets or reputation.

RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Intelligence Collection & Source Management

· Develop and maintain an approved intelligence collection plan aligned to site security risks.

· Gather information through lawful sources, observations, incident data, access-control records, open-source information and approved stakeholder networks.

· Assess source reliability and information credibility before dissemination.

· Protect source identities and sensitive information in accordance with authorisation and confidentiality requirements.

2. Intelligence Analysis & Threat Assessment

· Collate and analyse information to identify patterns, linkages, vulnerabilities and emerging threats.

· Prepare threat assessments, risk alerts, incident profiles, trend reports and intelligence briefs.

· Maintain threat registers, hotspot maps, subject or entity records and intelligence action logs.

· Translate findings into practical recommendations for security deployment and risk controls.

3. Support to Investigations

· Provide intelligence support for theft, fraud, collusion, illegal mining, access breaches, vandalism and other security incidents.

· Develop timelines, association charts and incident linkages using verified information.

· Assist with interview preparation and the identification of relevant records, witnesses and evidence sources.

· Maintain the integrity, confidentiality and traceability of intelligence and investigation records.

4.Surveillance & Operational Support

· Support authorised surveillance, observation and information-gathering activities in line with approved procedures.

· Provide pre-operational intelligence for patrols, escorts, searches, access-control operations and special security interventions.

· Monitor identified high-risk areas, routes, assets and activities and escalate material threats promptly.

· Participate in operational debriefs and capture lessons for future risk mitigation.

5. Stakeholder & Law-Enforcement Liaison

· Maintain professional working relationships with approved internal stakeholders, security business partners and relevant law-enforcement structures.

· Exchange information only through authorised channels and within legal and company requirements.

· Support joint threat assessments and coordinated responses when authorised by the Security Coordinator.

· Record material engagements, information requests and commitments.

6. Information Governance & Confidentiality

· Maintain secure intelligence files, databases, registers and distribution records.

· Apply need-to-know, access-control, retention and secure-disposal principles to sensitive information.

· Ensure information gathering and processing complies with POPIA, RICA, applicable criminal law, PSIRA requirements and company policies.

· Immediately report suspected information compromise, conflicts of interest or unethical conduct.

7.Reporting & Early Warning

· Issue timely intelligence alerts where credible threats require immediate action.

· Compile daily, weekly and monthly intelligence products and contribute to security dashboards and KPI reporting.

· Track changes in threat level and the effectiveness of implemented controls.

· Brief the Security Coordinator and authorised stakeholders clearly, objectively and without unsupported conclusions.

8. Security Risk & Control Assurance

· Support security risk assessments, vulnerability reviews and control testing.

· Identify gaps in physical security, access control, contractor controls, asset movement and information protection.

· Monitor agreed intelligence-related actions and provide evidence for closure.

· Participate in audits and provide accurate, auditable records.

9.Community, ESG & Human Rights

  • Monitor security-related social risks and community developments through lawful and approved channels.

  • Ensure intelligence activities respect human rights, dignity and company ESG commitments.

  • Avoid discriminatory profiling and base assessments on verified conduct, events and risk indicators.

  • Refer grievances or community matters through the appropriate governance channels.

10. Safety, Health & Environmental Compliance

  • Comply with the Mine Health and Safety Act, site rules, critical controls and Zero Harm requirements.

  • Participate in risk assessments, incident reviews, emergency exercises and required safety engagements.

  • Plan field activities with appropriate authorisation, communication and personal safety controls.

  • Perform any other reasonable security-intelligence duties within the scope and grade of the role.

QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS

Qualifications

· National Diploma or equivalent NQF Level 6 qualification in Security Management, Policing, Criminology, Forensic Investigation, Risk Management or a related field.

· PSIRA registration at Grade B or higher, where applicable to the position.

· Recognised intelligence analysis, investigation, interviewing, surveillance or forensic training is advantageous.

· Valid driver’s licence and medical fitness for the operational environment.

Experience

· At least 4–6 years’ relevant experience in security intelligence, crime intelligence, investigations or protective security, preferably in mining, industrial or critical-infrastructure operations.

· Practical experience in information verification, threat assessment, incident analysis and intelligence reporting.

· Experience working with multidisciplinary stakeholders and, where authorised, law-enforcement agencies.

· Experience handling confidential information and maintaining secure case or intelligence records.

Technical Competence

· Intelligence cycle: direction, collection, collation, evaluation, analysis, dissemination and review.

· Threat and vulnerability assessment, trend analysis, link analysis, timeline development and intelligence briefing.

· Investigation support, evidence awareness, chain-of-custody principles and records management.

· Working knowledge of POPIA, RICA, the Criminal Procedure Act, PSIRA requirements, the Mine Health and Safety Act and applicable company procedures.

· Competence in Microsoft Office, structured reporting, databases and approved security systems.

Behavioural

· High integrity, discretion and respect for confidentiality.

· Objective, analytical and evidence-based judgement.

· Clear written and verbal communication, including concise briefings.

· Alert, observant, methodical and able to prioritise under operational pressure.

· Professional stakeholder engagement and appropriate assertiveness.

· Respect for human rights, lawful conduct and non-discriminatory security practice.

Organisational Fit

· Demonstrates the Vedanta Group Values 2.0 framework (CIIAO): Care, Integrity, Innovation, Agility and Ownership.

· Supports a safe, secure and ESG-compliant operating environment.

· Protects confidential information and exercises sound judgement within delegated authority.

· Builds trusted working relationships without compromising independence or objectivity.

· Delivers accurate, timely and actionable intelligence products.

title: Jobrådgivere/koordinerende sagsbehandlere til Jobcenter København - Center for Beskæftigelse og Afklaring
description:
Vil du arbejde med at hjælpe udsatte ledige ud på arbejdsmarkedet?

I Center for Beskæftigelse og Afklaring tror vi på, at der er plads til flere på arbejdsmarkedet og søger i den forbindelse ambitiøse, handlekraftige og kreativt tænkende medarbejdere, der deler vores overbevisning om, at selv en begrænset deltagelse på det ordinære arbejdsmarked giver mening og værdi for det enkelte menneske. Vi søger nu medarbejdere til flere forskellige afdelinger, der alle er organiseret i samme center, men har variationer i opgaveløsning.

Vi søger medarbejdere, der skal arbejde med borgere i målgrupperne: kontanthjælp, ressourceforløb og ledighedsydelse. Vores opgave er at arbejde med virksomhedsplaceringer, formidling af ordinære job samt småjobs/lønnede timer for at udvikle arbejdsevnen – eller hjælpe til afklaring af samme, med henblik på at kunne træffe afgørelse om tilkendelse af fleksjob eller førtidspension.

Du vil komme til at arbejde i en afdeling med ca. 30 kollegaer og have adgang til en bred vifte af faglig sparring. Vi arbejder med systematisk fokus på fremdrift og progression i sagerne.

Vi står midt i en beskæftigelsesreform og kigger derfor ind i en fremtid med spændende forandringer i vores arbejde med de udsatte ledige. Det kalder på omstillingsparathed, hvor vi ikke har alle svarene – og du henter din energi i præcis de rammer.

Om opgaven som jobrådgiver/koordinerende sagsbehandler
Dine arbejdsopgaver vil koncentrere sig om en kontinuerlig indsats overfor cirka 30 ledige borgere. Som jobrådgiver/koordinerende sagsbehandler vil du både skulle fungere som myndighedsperson og virksomhedskonsulent for alle dine borgere, og du skal arbejde med gruppeforløb, hvor vi samler flere borgere i en fælles faglig indsats med fokus på at understøtte borgerne i deres vej mod arbejdsmarkedet. Derudover skal du forberede sagen ift., at der kan træffes afgørelse om fleksjob og førtidspension, når det er relevant.

Særligt om at arbejde fremskudt
For at lykkedes med vores opgave, er det en forudsætning, at vi arbejder både helhedsorienteret og tværfagligt. Derfor arbejdes der i særligt to af vores afdelinger fremskudt, hvilket betyder at man som jobrådgiver/sagsbehandler arbejder på lokationer bl.a. i Socialforvaltningen, den ambulante psykiatri og i Danmarks Fængsler. Her er det vigtigt at have blik for, hvordan man investerer i samarbejdsrelationen. Det fremskudte samarbejde indebærer løbende møder og opfølgning ude hos samarbejdspartnerne med og uden borgere, hvor indsatsen for borgerne tilrettelægges i fællesskab. For så vidt angår arbejdet med Danmarks Fængsler arbejder vi kontinuerligt på at bygge bro mellem indsættelse og frihed.

At være fremskudt medarbejder indebærer altså et tæt samarbejde med kontaktpersoner, myndighedssagsbehandlere, gadeplansmedarbejdere mv. om egne borgere. Derudover skal du bygge bro mellem Socialforvaltningen og kollegaer i Beskæftigelses, Integrations og Erhvervsforvaltningen - også om borgere, du ikke er jobrådgiver/sagsbehandler for.

Din profil

  • Du ved, ligesom vi, at for at hjælpe borgere væk fra offentlig forsørgelse er det nødvendigt med en vedholdende og målrettet indsats, der er koncentreret om en kobling til det ordinære arbejdsmarked.
  • Du tror på, at en god relation til den samme jobrådgiver/koordinerende sagsbehandler har en afgørende værdi for borgeren og derfor også for samarbejdet omkring at nå det fælles mål, som er tilknytning til arbejdsmarkedet.
  • Du har forståelse for, og gerne erfaring med, at virksomhedsplaceringer kan etableres på en konstruktiv måde og sideløbende med andre typer af indsatser overfor borgere med komplekse problemstillinger.
  • Du ved, at det gode individuelle match mellem borger og virksomhed er en forudsætning for et positivt forløb.

Følgende formelle/faglige kompetencer bliver prioriteret

  • Har kendskab til målgruppen – udsatte ledige
  • Kan strukturere og prioritere egne arbejdsopgaver med mange forskellige opgaver og dagsordener – herunder håndtere egen sagsstamme på 30 borgere.
  • Er struktureret og har en god skriftlighed i sagsarbejdet.
  • Har evner til at identificere og anerkende virksomheders behov og kendskab til arbejdet med virksomhedsplaceringer.
  • Er i stand til at skabe udvikling, motivation og fremdrift for de borgere, du samarbejder med, og ligeledes er i stand til at dokumentere den indsats, der igangsættes for den enkelte borger
  • Har stærke IT-kompetencer, systemforståelse og god datadisciplin (vi arbejder i Fasit)
  • Kan indgå og trives med en anerkendende samarbejdskultur, hvor vi med venlighed og ordentlighed tager ansvar for den fælles opgaveløsning

Vi vægter derudover følgende personlige kompetencer højt

  • Faglig selvtillid, hvilket afspejles i dine samarbejdsevner og resultater
  • Evne til at arbejde reflekteret med nærhed og distance i relationsarbejdet
  • Er udholdende, kan sadle om og søge nye løsninger
  • Det falder dig naturligt at søge (og give) sparring som en del af din opgaveløsning

Vi tilbyder

  • Ansættelse i en udviklingsorienteret organisation, under stadig forandring.
  • Dygtige og engagerede kollegaer i et godt socialt miljø
  • Faglig ledelse, ambitiøse mål og gode rammer til at nå dem
  • Oplæring og introduktion til arbejdspladsen og opgaverne herunder deltagelse i Beskæftigelses-, Integrations- og Erhvervsforvaltningens uddannelse (BIF-uddannelsen) – en kompetencegivende uddannelse indenfor beskæftigelse (ECTS-givende).
  • Løbende kompetenceudvikling gennem kurser og faglig sparring
  • Personalegoder: Flekstid, Meyers kantine, frugtordning, massageordning og fitnessrum på arbejdspladsen.

Ansættelsesforhold
Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår er efter overenskomst mellem Kommunernes Landsforening og HK/Kommunal for vejledere/undervisere indenfor beskæftigelsesområdet i Københavns Kommune eller Dansk Socialrådgiverforening. Lønnen er efter principperne om Ny Løn.

Der er tale om både faste og midlertidige stillinger. Vi ønsker stillingerne besat hurtigst muligt eller efter aftale.

Mere information
Hvis du vil vide mere om stillingerne eller har andre spørgsmål, kan du kontakte afdelingschef Katrine Richter på 51 72 72 48 eller Anna Rasmussen på 2313 00 85.

Er du specifikt interesseret i at arbejde med Danmarks Fængsler, kan du kontakte afdelingschef Sara Sigrid Lund 26 33 38 32.

Søg via linket senest fredag den 20. november 2026
Vi afholder løbende samtaler.

Om Beskæftigelses- Integrations- og Erhvervsforvaltningen
I Beskæftigelses-, Integrations- og Erhvervsforvaltningen hjælper vi hver dag året rundt københavnere i job og uddannelse eller finder andre veje videre for borgerne. Vi understøtter virksomhederne med at finde den rette arbejdskraft. Vi inddrager borgerne, stiller konstruktive krav, og vi tror på, at vi sammen kan skabe fremskridt. Vi er Danmarks største beskæftigelsesforvaltning, og vi er med til at sætte en høj standard på beskæftigelsesområdet ved at arbejde strategisk med udvikling af driften, servicedesign og nye digitale løsninger. Vi har fokus på trivsel og har en kultur med høj faglighed, hvor der er plads til dine input og idéer.

title: Interim Service Manager - SENA
description:
Organisation: Leicestershire County Council

Work Location: County Hall Glenfield LE3 8RA

Salary: £65,109 -71,631 per annum ( Pro rata for part time)

Working Hours: 37 Hours per week

Contract Type: Fixed term for (24 Months) Or Secondment for (24 Months) With Managers permission

Closing Date: 26th November2026

Interview Date(s): TBC 9th Dec 2026

Make an impact. Shape the future of Post-16 SEND in Leicestershire.

We are looking for an experienced, ambitious and collaborative leader to join Leicestershire’s SENA Service at an exciting point in its development.

This Service Manager role will have a particular leadership focus on our Post-16 SENA Team, providing senior oversight of our work with young people as they move through further education and towards adulthood. You will work closely and collaboratively with colleges, Post-16 providers, education, health, social care and other partners to strengthen pathways and support effective transitions for young people with SEND.

A key priority will be ensuring that preparation for adulthood is at the heart of our work, supporting a stronger focus on young people's aspirations, independence, employment, community participation and adult lives, alongside the effective delivery of our statutory EHCP responsibilities.

You may bring substantial experience from SENA or statutory SEND services, or you may come from a strong Post-16 background, including further education, transitions and preparation for adulthood. What matters is your ability to lead complex services, inspire people, build strong partnerships and maintain a clear focus on improving outcomes for young people.

Why join us?

Leicestershire’s SENA Service is diverse, ambitious, innovative, creative and forward-thinking. We want people who bring ideas, challenge us to improve and work collaboratively to find better solutions.

Partnership and co-production are central to how we work. We work closely with our Parent Carer Forum, SEND Hub, and our Strategic Young People’s Group, ensuring that children, young people and families have a meaningful voice in shaping our services.

Most importantly, the children and young people of Leicestershire matter to us. We want young people with SEND to have high aspirations for their future and to be supported to move into adulthood with the greatest possible opportunity for independence, employment, relationships, community participation and a fulfilling adult life.

This two-year opportunity gives you enough time to make a real impact, build relationships across the Post-16 sector, lead meaningful change and see the results of your work. It also provides an excellent opportunity to broaden your senior leadership experience and take the next step in your career.

About the Role

  • Provide strategic leadership of the Post-16 SENA Team.
  • Drive improvements in Post-16 EHCPs, annual reviews, transitions, and preparation for adulthood.
  • Build effective partnerships with colleges and Post-16 providers to improve outcomes for young people with SEND.
  • Lead and develop staff, promoting high standards, accountability, and performance.
  • Ensure young people's aspirations and adult life outcomes are central to decision-making.
  • Work across education, health, and social care to support successful transitions to adulthood.
  • Contribute to SEND sufficiency, commissioning, High Needs funding, and budget management.
  • Oversee complex cases, mediation, tribunals, and complaints.
  • Champion co-production and the voice of young people and their families.

An enhanced DBS with barred list check is required for this post.

For information on our approach to the recruitment of ex-offenders, please see our policy statement

About You

To apply for this post, you must be able to evidence in your application how you meet the following criteria:

  • A management qualification, evidence of continued learning and development, and demonstrable, fully evidenced experience of developing, managing and delivering an effective service relevant to this level of responsibility.
  • Significant relevant experience within SEND, Post-16 education or a closely related service for children and young people, together with strong knowledge and understanding of SEND legislation, statutory guidance, national policy and the legislative and governance framework associated with SEND.
  • Substantial senior management and leadership experience within a complex service, including managing staff and other resources, strategic thinking, and successfully leading significant and demanding programmes of organisational and service change.
  • Proven experience of developing and delivering high-quality services in accordance with statutory requirements and strategic organisational priorities, including strong performance management and reporting and the ability to research, analyse and use information and data to inform service improvement, recommendations and service planning.
  • Excellent communication, partnership, influencing and negotiation skills, including significant experience of working with and influencing partners to deliver change, communicating complex information effectively to different audiences and building effective relationships at all levels.
  • Strong experience and understanding of resource management, including High Needs funding and commissioning requirements, with a successful track record of planning and delivering change within agreed timescales and budgets and securing organisational efficiencies where possible.
  • Proven ability to operate effectively within a complex and demanding environment, including managing a heavy workload and competing priorities, identifying and managing risk and interdependencies, solving complex problems, appropriately challenging established practice, extensive experience of managing staff and other resources. Motivating others and demonstrating a clear commitment to improving outcomes for children and young people.

In addition, we also expect you to share our commitment to our values and to delivering accessible and inclusive services which meet the needs of all of our residents. You will be asked to demonstrate your understanding of these commitments as part of the selection process.

Reasonable adjustments will be considered for applicants with a disability. We are a Disability Confident Employer.

Please note: If you are appointed to this role on a fixed-term or internal secondment basis, you may later be offered a permanent appointment to the role, should the opportunity become available. Any such arrangements will be subject to organisational requirements and the relevant policy conditions being met.

Interested in Flexible Working?

Michelle White Head of Service - SEND & Children with Disabilities

At Leicestershire County Council we’re looking for top talent from all walks of life. title: System Validation Engineer
description:
Summary:

The System Validation Engineer is tasked with ensuring the integrity and functionality of automotive systems through systematic testing and validation. This role is crucial in achieving the organization's objectives concerning delivery, quality, and cost.

Responsibilities:

  • System Validation tests pattern/sequences creation and execution according to the defined strategy in line with test standards.
  • Design, review and execute test cases for requirements defined by System architecture.
  • Perform scenario-based testing, result analysis, and defect reporting.
  • Design, review and execute test cases for Technical Safety Concept/System Requirement (ISO 26262) in alignment with System architecture requirements.
  • Define system automation test strategy using an internally defined Test automation environment.
  • Review and verify System Architecture Design from a testability perspective.
  • Ensure traceability from System Architecture, including System Interfaces and Technical Safety concepts, to the System Test Cases.
  • Design, review and execute System Test Cases according to the Test Plan and define strategies.
  • Implement automated test cases in the defined Automated Test Environment.
  • Generate System Test Reports in line with Forvia Standards.
  • Perform re-use analysis effectively across the system test scope of work.
  • Open System defects and track their progress for closure effectively.
  • Define the test environment and needed instrumentation to execute System Test Cases.

Must Haves:

  • Bachelor of Engineering degree in Electronics/Electrical.
  • 3 to 8 years’ experience in Seat/Cluster/ADAS Validation.
  • Relevant understanding of key automotive system areas: CAN, Ethernet, CAPL, python.
  • Knowledge of product architecture (Infotainment, Cluster, ADAS, etc.)
  • Strong grasp of ASPICE and Agile methodology.
  • Capability to analyze system requirements and architecture.
  • Able to drive test case creation and test script execution.
  • Experience with Requirements Management Tools (ALM, Interenterprise Architect) and Atlassian Suite (Jira, Confluence).
  • Hands-on experience with Toolchain: Vector Canoe, VT system, Vteststudio, V-Flash DIVA.
  • Experience with communication protocols: 100BT1, 10BT1S, DOIP, SomeIP, TCP, UDP.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience working in a Scrum team in Agile methodology.
  • Experience in Software Testing Life Cycle (STLC).
  • Experience in ASPICE SYS4 & SYS5.
  • Experience in Vehicle Testing.

Other Details:

  • Category 1: Location - Not specified.
  • Category 2: Team Structure - Part of the System Validation team.
  • Category 3: Reporting - Not specified.

Reason (Must Have):

  • Bachelor of Engineering: Critical for understanding electronic and electrical principles necessary for validation tasks.
  • Experience in Validation: Essential for executing specific industry-related validations effectively.
  • Understanding of automotive systems: Required to effectively test and validate various components within automotive systems.
  • Knowledge of ASPICE, Agile: Necessary for adhering to industry-standard methodologies and ensuring quality outputs.
  • Capability to analyze architecture: Important for developing relevant test cases and ensuring compliance with requirements.
  • Experience with automation tools: Essential for increasing the efficiency of the testing process.
  • Hands-on experience with protocols: Crucial for ensuring communication integrity within automotive systems.

Reason (Nice to Have):

  • Experience in Scrum: Useful for enhancing collaborative team dynamics and agile project management.
  • Knowledge of STLC: Adds value in efficiently managing the testing process.
  • Understanding of ASPICE SYS4 & SYS5: Provides deeper insights that can improve the validation process.
  • Experience in Vehicle Testing: Beneficial for contextualizing system validation in real-world scenarios.

Trust Score:

Score: High
Evidence: Detailed responsibilities and specific technologies are clearly outlined, aiding effective candidate sourcing.

Sourcing Guidance:

The job description provides good technical clarity for sourcing. Consider these potential recommendations to enhance the search:

  1. Recommendation: Search for candidates with experience in ADAS systems alongside general automotive validation skills.
    Rationale: These skills are often paired in roles focused on advanced driver-assistance systems.
  2. Recommendation: Look for candidates who have worked in automotive software environments and are familiar with regulatory standards.
    Rationale: This knowledge will add value to compliance during system validation processes.
  3. Recommendation: Consider flexible requirements around protocol experiences, allowing candidates with some experience in CAN or Ethernet, but not both, to apply.
    Rationale: This may broaden the pool of qualified candidates significantly.

title: Director of Finance and Risk Management - Rabat, Morocco
description:
Summary: Counterpart International is currently seeking a Director of Finance and Risk Management (DFRM) to support the USDA Food for Progress (FFPr) Promoting Rural Infrastructure, Modernization, and Efficiency (PRIME) project. The overall objective of the project is to modernize Morocco's slaughterhouse and cold-chain infrastructure across the livestock value chain, contributing to improved food safety, market efficiency, agricultural productivity, and trade. Aligned with Morocco's Generation Green 2030 strategy and USDA Food for Progress objectives, PRIME will strengthen regulatory compliance, build institutional and workforce capacity, facilitate public and private investment, and improve market access through enhanced traceability and consumer awareness.

In collaboration with the Chief of Party (COP), the DFRM will oversee all the operational and financial aspects of the project, ensuring that financial operations are in compliance with USDA regulations. In addition, the DFRM will carry out the below responsibilities. This is a full-time position based in Rabat, and will report to Chief of Party. Qualified Moroccan nationals are encouraged to apply.

Primary Responsibilities

Financial

· As the primary responsible person for the financial management of the project, ensure accounting books are closed by the required deadline and all monthly-financial-report documentation are thoroughly checked, signed/approved and submitted to DC Office Project Finance Officer in charge.

· Monitor program budget burn rate and update information monthly related to project budget, pipelines, accruals, financial reports, and spending projections, in coordination with Programs.

· Prepare monthly requests for funds from the US office to ensure the project has the necessary funds for operations

· Manage the relationship with the local bank and ensure smooth program implementation and accurate financial operations

· Prepare quarterly cash advance requests to USDA for submission by the US office

· Work closely with the COP to manage high-risk issues and potential financial liabilities. Escalate any high-risk issues to Counterpart HQ.

· Establish and oversee financial management systems, procedures, and controls.

· Acquire mastery of Counterpart Field Finance Operations Manual, Procurement Manual, Grants Manual, Accounting QuickBooks Manual and other relevant operations and administrative documents.

· Provide regular training to financial and administrative staff on tools, policies and procedures to increase efficiency in project operations.

· Work with US office to develop the project Finance, Human Resources, Procurement, Risk and other manuals and update them as necessary.

· Carry out internal compliance assessments to ensure that Counterpart and donor guidelines are implemented and upheld and that the findings are captured in the risk register/issues log

· Coordinate all necessary audits, statutory requirements, and financial enquiries from USDA, the Government of Morocco and HQ; including tax reporting as required by local law

· Review the monthly tax return and the annual income tax and VAT affidavit if applicable.

· Review and supervise the payroll of social benefits and income withholdings

· Supervise the sending of pay slips, payroll books and accounting books in accordance with the established policies and procedures

· Supervise the registration in the accounting system of all transactions carried out in accordance with the accounting procedures established by the US office

· Send accounting information to the central office on the dates indicated monthly.

Operations & Administration

· Manage and oversee all operations related to the project, including logistical, procurement, security, access, human resources, risk and compliance and ensure compliance with Morocco laws, Counterpart policies and donor regulations.

· Ensure that operational systems are in place and that they perform optimally in support of the timely implementation of field activities.

· Supervise and support the contracting and execution of all logistical coordination, transportation, purchase of equipment, purchase of inputs, and leasing of equipment for the proper development of all activities.

· Oversee all aspects of HR management, including the development of HR policies, recruitment, and compliance with local labor law.

· Supervise and support the contracting of medical, life and vehicle insurance and the execution of contracts.

· Conduct partner capacity assessments and flag high-risk concerns to management; ensure a mechanism is in place to monitor compliance by sub-contracted partners.

· Coordinate weekly internal coordination meetings with senior staff and ensure proper dissemination of information to all staff as appropriate.

· Ensure program implementation follows Counterpart’s policies/procedures, the laws of the Government of Morocco, and USDA rules and regulations, particularly with respect to financial and grants management.

· Oversee the relationship with the legal and accounting firms and ensure all requirements are duly met

· Ensure registration requirements are met each year and registration renewal is documented

· Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

· Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance, or equivalent; Master’s degree preferred.

· Minimum of 8 years of relevant work experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, with a minimum of 4 years of progressively responsible finance and operational management experience backstopping USG-Funded programs.

· Experience working and leading Finance and Operations teams to deliver project objectives.

· Knowledge of applicable US government regulations.

· Proven experience managing the finances of large ($10M+) projects.

· Demonstrated ability to implement financial systems for development projects.

· Strong analytical and computer skills, especially with accounting software, spreadsheets, and in financial analysis.

· Demonstrated project management experience, including budget and financial management.

· At least 3 years’ experience managing risk and compliance with an international NGO.

· Demonstrated ability to give effective presentations and write high-quality technical reports.

· Ability to produce high-quality deliverables throughout the project cycle from planning, management, and execution to troubleshooting.

· Demonstrated ability to communicate fully and effectively, both orally and in writing, in English, Arabic, and Amazigh is required; proficiency in French is preferred.

Counterpart is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer and does not discriminate in its selection and employment practices. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, age, or other legally protected characteristics.

As an Art Instructor, you'll bring meaningful artistic experiences directly to local elementary schools, helping children develop creative skills, confidence, and self-expression. You'll also play an important role in building a sustainable, high-demand art enrichment program that families value, students look forward to, and schools are excited to offer.

What You'll Do

You'll lead engaging classes in drawing, painting, clay, collage, mixed media, printmaking, and other creative techniques. Through age-appropriate projects and instruction, you'll introduce students to artistic fundamentals while encouraging imagination, exploration, and individual expression.

You'll develop structured, progressive lessons that build skills throughout each program session. Your ability to balance creative freedom with meaningful instruction will help students develop confidence and take pride in their accomplishments.

You'll create a welcoming environment where beginners feel comfortable experimenting and more experienced young artists can continue developing their abilities.

You'll also prepare materials, organize supplies, supervise students, maintain attendance, and build positive relationships with children, families, school staff, and program leadership. You may also help coordinate student artwork displays and end-of-session family showcases.

What We're Looking For

We're seeking someone with direct experience teaching art to elementary-aged children who enjoys sharing their artistic knowledge and encouraging young learners.

Candidates should have a strong understanding of artistic fundamentals and experience working with multiple art mediums. Experience in elementary art education, community art programs, youth enrichment, or school-based instruction is highly valued.

Ideal candidates are creative, patient, dependable, organized, and comfortable adapting lessons for different ages, learning styles, and artistic abilities.

Strong classroom management, positive guidance, and the ability to create engaging, age-appropriate learning experiences are essential.

Spanish-speaking or bilingual (English/Spanish) abilities are a plus and would be valuable when communicating with students and families.

Applicants must be at least 18, have reliable transportation between assigned schools, and complete required background screening and youth safety training.

CPR/First Aid certification is preferred.

Help inspire the next generation of artists, creators, and imaginative thinkers!

title: Mocap TD - MoEdit
description:
The Mocap TD - MoEdit is responsible for developing and supporting the technical workflows, pipeline integrations and tools used to transform motion capture data into production-ready Motion Edit shots.
The role focuses on building efficient workflows for combining retargeted motion, layout and camera data; developing tools for shot and crowd Motion Edit work; and ensuring that Mocap and Motion Edit integrate effectively into the wider production pipeline.
Candidates may be based in the UK, North America or Europe but must be willing and able to travel to India and work on set and with the wider team.
Key Responsibilities
Shot-Building Pipeline
  • Develop and maintain workflows for constructing Motion Edit shots from retargeted motion, layout, camera data, props and associated scene data where required.
  • Ensure shot-building processes are reliable, repeatable and scalable.
  • Reduce unnecessary manual setup and technical overhead for artists.
  • Motion Edit Tools
  • Develop tools supporting Motion Edit workflows for individual shots and crowd work.
  • Identify repetitive or error-prone processes suitable for automation.
Pipeline Integration
  • Supervise the technical integration of Mocap and Motion Edit data into the production pipeline.
  • Work with Pipeline and Technology teams to define requirements for Motion Edit workflows.
  • Ensure output is compatible with downstream Animation, Layout and CG processes.
  • Identify and resolve technical issues affecting the transfer and usability of motion data.
Performance & Quality Improvement
  • Develop technical solutions that increase the speed and quality of animation delivery.
  • Profile workflow bottlenecks and recommend technical improvements.
  • Support artists and supervisors with complex technical troubleshooting.
  • Contribute to continuous development of Motion Edit pipeline standards and best practices.
  • Provide technical readiness and dependency information to the Global Motion Capture Producer so priorities and handoffs can be coordinated effectively.
Must have
  • Demonstrated expertise in developing and managing post-production workflows, including retargeting, motion editing, shot assembly and pipeline tooling to support end-to-end cinematic production.
  • Extensive experience working within a large-scale motion capture studio, developing and delivering robust workflows, pipelines and tools to support high-volume, high-intensity capture environments.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with Vicon (setup, capture and processing), Xsens, head-mounted camera systems and MotionBuilder.
  • Strong proficiency in Python, with proven experience developing tools to optimise mocap workflows and enhance pipeline efficiency.
  • Proven experience overseeing the development, implementation and ongoing support of animation pipelines, from retargeting and motion editing through to final delivery for crowds, vignettes and individual shots.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to Mumbai, working both on set and work with the wider team, with the schedule to be confirmed.
  • Proven experience working within a global organisation, managing geographically dispersed teams, multiple motion capture studio locations and concurrent projects while maintaining consistent technical and operational standards.
About you
  • A confident and effective communicator, able to collaborate seamlessly across creative, technical and management teams, engaging with stakeholders at all levels of the business.
  • A proactive and resourceful problem-solver, with the ability to navigate complex creative and technical challenges and deliver practical, innovative solutions.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, consistently maintaining high standards of accuracy, quality and efficiency.
  • Highly adaptable and responsive, with the ability to navigate changing priorities and challenges in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Highly organised, thoughtful and pragmatic, with a structured, solutions-focused approach to planning, decision-making and delivering results.

title: Intake and Assessment Officer
description:
Be the person who helps someone take their first step towards better mental health.

At the Lismore Medicare Mental Health Centre, every conversation has the potential to change a life. As an Intake & Assessment Officer, you'll be one of the first people individuals, families and carers connect with when seeking support, providing compassionate guidance, clinical assessment and access to the services they need.

This is a rewarding opportunity to join a passionate multidisciplinary team that is committed to delivering accessible, person-centred mental health care for the local community. Working alongside clinicians, GPs, community engagement professionals and support staff, you'll play a pivotal role in helping people navigate their mental health journey while ensuring they feel heard, supported and connected.

Why Join Us?

You'll be joining a welcoming, collaborative and purpose-driven team where your expertise is valued and your development is supported.

What's On Offer?

· Permanent Full-Time opportunity or 0.6 FTE

· Meaningful work supporting people experiencing mental health challenges

· Work within a multidisciplinary team delivering integrated care

· Salary packaging benefits: up to $15,900 tax-free plus $2,650 meals and entertainment.

· Access to employee discounts across shopping, dining, and travel.

What You'll Be Doing

· Conduct intake, screening, assessment and risk evaluations for people accessing the service

· Provide brief interventions, care coordination and referrals to appropriate supports

· Develop collaborative care plans and support people to access the services they need

· Work closely with local health, community and partner organisations to deliver holistic care

· Participate in case reviews, clinical discussions and regular supervision

· Contribute to the positive reputation and growth of the Medicare Mental Health Centre within the community

· Work a regular fortnightly weekend roster as part of service delivery

About You

You're passionate about supporting people through challenging periods in their lives and have the confidence to assess needs, identify risks and coordinate appropriate supports. You combine clinical capability with genuine empathy and build trust quickly with people from all walks of life.

To be successful, you'll bring:

· Qualifications in health, mental health, community services, behavioural/social sciences or a related discipline

· Experience conducting intake, screening, biopsychosocial and risk assessments, with strong knowledge of recovery-oriented mental health practice

· Proven ability to coordinate care and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams

· Exceptional communication skills with the ability to build relationships with clients, families, carers and service providers

· Strong organisational, time management and computer skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and use clinical systems, databases and Microsoft Office applications

About the Centre

The Medicare Mental Health Centre provides free and accessible mental health support in a welcoming environment where people can access information, assessment, referral pathways and ongoing assistance. As part of our team, you'll help ensure people receive the right support at the right time, when they need it most.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you're looking for a role where you can combine your clinical skills with meaningful community impact, we'd love to hear from you. Applications will be reviewed as they're received, so don't wait to apply.

Questions? Contact Charissa Foster at charissa.foster@vertaview.org.au

Diversity is Strength. We strongly encourage applications from First Nations peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and those with lived or peer mental health experience.

title: Engagement Manager (HCM Implementation, People Manager)
description:
About Darwinbox

Darwinboxis Asia's fastest-growing HR technology platform, designing the future of work by building the world's best HR tech, driven by a fierce focus on employee experience and customer success, and continuous, iterative innovation. We are the preferred choice of 1000+ global enterprises to manage their 4 million+ employees across 130+ countries. Darwinbox's new-age HCM suite competes with local as well as global players in the enterprise technology space (such as SAP, Oracle, and Workday). The firm has acquired notable customers ranging from large conglomerates to unicorn start-ups: Nivea, Starbucks, DLF, JSW, Adani Group, Crisil, CRED, Vedanta, Mahindra, Glenmark, Gokongwei Group, Mitra Adiperkasa, EFS Facilities Management, VNG Corporation, and many more. Our vision of building a world-class product company from Asia is backed by marquee global investors like Microsoft, Salesforce, Sequoia Capital, TCV, KKR, and Partners Group.


What this role is

Darwinbox is transforming how enterprises manage people, workflows, and employee experiences at scale. As we evolve, implementation is no longer about configuration and delivery tracking. The real challenge is helping organizations rethink how HR should operate across systems, processes, adoption, and decision-making.

This role sits at the intersection of:

  • Enterprise consulting

  • Product thinking

  • Customer transformation

  • Large-scale SaaS delivery

You will act as:

  • A trusted advisor to enterprise customers

  • A strategic partner to CHROs and business leaders

  • The “Voice of Customer” internally across Product and Engineering

  • An owner responsible for customer outcomes — not just go-live milestones

What the work looks like

  • You won’t just inherit a project plan. You’ll inherit ambiguity.

  • A customer struggling to standardize processes globally.

  • An implementation that technically works, but operationally doesn’t.

  • A workflow designed for manual operations that now needs to scale intelligently.

Your role is to understand the business problem behind the requirement and drive the transformation end-to-end.

That means:

  • Leading enterprise HCM transformation programs from discovery through adoption

  • Challenging legacy processes and driving transformation conversations

  • Influencing senior stakeholders with clarity and credibility

  • Working closely with internal teams to shape customer outcomes

  • Balancing customer expectations, scalability, product capabilities, and operational realities

Because enterprise transformation breaks when those worlds operate separately.

Who thrives here

  • People who think in systems.

  • People who naturally ask: “Will this scale?” / “What breaks after go-live?” / “Are we solving the actual customer problem?”

  • People with consulting instincts, strong ownership mindset, and executive presence.

  • People who care equally about customer outcomes, product experience, and operational excellence.

What we explicitly don’t optimize for

  • Coordination-heavy implementation profiles

  • Delivery managers who only track timelines

  • Requirement takers who never challenge assumptions

  • Governance without ownership

  • Implementation thinking without business context

What we’re looking for

  • 6–12 years of experience in enterprise SaaS, HCM implementation, consulting, or transformation roles

  • Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills

  • Consulting mindset with ability to drive transformation conversations

  • Strong customer advocacy and product-oriented thinking

  • Data-driven and automation-first approach to problem solving

Lastly, what we are not looking for , we’re not looking for traditional implementation managers nor project coordinators and definitely not people who measure success by whether the tracker is green.

title: Application & AI Delivery Manager (Remote)
description:
American Specialty Health Incorporated (ASH) is seeking an Application & AI Delivery Manager to join our Information Technology Operations department. The Application & AI Delivery Manager is a business-facing leadership role responsible for bridging the gap between business stakeholders and technology teams. This role serves as the primary relationship owner and strategic advisor to business leaders, helping them identify, evaluate, and realize value from application, automation, and AI-enabled solutions that advance organizational objectives.

Acting as a trusted partner to the business, this role leads stakeholders through the full solution lifecycle—from discovery and intake through delivery, adoption, and measured outcomes. The role owns the enterprise application intake process and guides requests through evaluation, governance, planning, and delivery, ensuring solutions move efficiently from concept to implementation while meeting organizational requirements for security, privacy, compliance, vendor management, and responsible AI governance.

This is a hybrid business and technical role. While the primary orientation is toward business partnership and value realization, the Application & AI Delivery Manager must also bring direct hands-on experience building and deploying AI productivity tools and AI agents. The role continuously improves intake, review, and delivery processes to provide a clear, consistent path for bringing technology solutions into the organization.

Salary Range

American Specialty Health complies with state and federal wage and hour laws and compensation depends upon candidate’s qualifications, education, skill set, years of experience, and internal equity. $89,300.00 to 118,000.00 Full-Time Annual Salary Range.



Remote Worker Guidelines

  • Remote Worker Guidelines: This position will be trained remotely and must be able to work from home (WFH) in a designated work area with company-provided technology equipment. This WFH position requires you have a stable connection to your Internet Service Provider with the ability to participate by video in online meetings over a reliable and consistent network. The internet connection must have a consistent 50 down/10 up Mbps minimum internet speed. 100 down/20 up is recommended to support higher quality video meetings.


Responsibilities

  • Business Partnership, Solution Discovery & Value Realization
    • Serve as the primary business relationship owner for application, automation, and AI initiatives, building trusted partnerships with business leaders and stakeholders across the organization.
    • Lead discovery engagements—including facilitated sessions, workflow assessments, and requirements-gathering activities—to deeply understand operational challenges, strategic priorities, and technology needs.
    • Guide business teams in identifying and evaluating appropriate solutions, including existing enterprise capabilities, application enhancements, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions.
    • Act as a trusted advisor to business leaders on the introduction of new applications, emerging technologies, and AI capabilities into the organization.
    • Connect business stakeholders with application, AI, integration, data, infrastructure, and other technical teams to assess solution options and develop actionable recommendations.
    • Collaborate with business partners to define success criteria, adoption goals, key performance indicators, and expected business outcomes for each initiative before work begins.
    • Help develop business cases, expected outcomes, success measures, and implementation approaches for proposed solutions.
    • Facilitate the identification of baseline measures and value metrics that can be used to evaluate application, automation, and AI initiatives.
    • Work with business stakeholders to establish methods for measuring operational improvements, productivity gains, cost avoidance, risk reduction, user experience improvements, and other targeted outcomes.
    • Coordinate communication, training, and change management activities to support successful adoption of new solutions.
    • Monitor implementation outcomes and stakeholder feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and course correction.
    • Develop reporting and visibility into realized benefits, adoption trends, and business outcomes across the application and AI solution portfolio.
    • Recommend enhancements, process improvements, or additional capabilities based on measured results and evolving business needs.
    • Provide leadership with clear visibility into the value delivered by technology initiatives and the progress of business outcome measurements.
  • Intake and Governance Management
    • Own and continuously improve the enterprise application and AI intake process.
    • Serve as the primary entry point for business requests involving new applications, technology capabilities, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions.
    • Evaluate incoming requests and determine the appropriate review path based on the nature of the request, associated risks, and organizational requirements.
    • Coordinate Application Governance, Vendor Oversight, Security Architecture Review, Legal, Privacy, Procurement, and AI governance activities as required.
    • Ensure reviews are appropriately scoped to the change or use case being introduced, balancing risk management with timely delivery.
    • Maintain intake standards, documentation, decision records, process metrics, and stakeholder communications.
    • Support the maintenance of the enterprise AI registry and application portfolio inventory.
  • Delivery Coordination and Enablement
    • Coordinate approved initiatives from intake through implementation, adoption, and transition to operational ownership.
    • Establish delivery plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and stakeholder commitments in partnership with business and technical teams.
    • Facilitate collaboration across business, engineering, architecture, security, infrastructure, vendor, and governance stakeholders.
    • Support testing, pilot activities, deployment readiness, go-live planning, and post-implementation stabilization.
    • Track progress, remove obstacles, and escalate issues that may impact successful delivery.
    • Ensure clear ownership and accountability throughout the solution lifecycle.
  • Continuous Improvement
    • Identify opportunities to improve intake, governance, and delivery processes.
    • Promote standardization, reuse of approved technologies, and reduction of unnecessary technology duplication.
    • Develop and maintain process documentation, templates, decision frameworks, and reporting metrics.
    • Partner with governance and technical stakeholders to streamline reviews and improve the stakeholder experience.
    • Maintain awareness of emerging technologies, application capabilities, automation opportunities, and AI advancements that may benefit the organization.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.


Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field preferred.
  • Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience required. If equivalent experience, a High School Diploma is required.
  • 5 years of experience in business relationship management, technology initiative leadership, product management, business analysis, or related disciplines required.
  • 1-3 years of demonstrated experience partnering with business leaders and stakeholders to identify needs, shape solutions, and drive measurable business outcomes required.
  • 1-3 years of experience with enterprise application governance, vendor management, or technology portfolio management preferred.
  • 1-3 years of experience leading AI, automation, and digital transformation initiatives with measurable business impact preferred.
  • 1-3 years of familiarity with security, privacy, compliance, and risk management processes preferred.
  • 1 year of experience in healthcare or regulated industries preferred.
  • 1-3 years of experience in Project Management, Product Management, or Business Analysis, or related professional certifications, preferred.
  • Proven ability to facilitate discovery sessions, requirements workshops, and cross-functional working sessions. (High proficiency)
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying AI productivity tools and AI agents in a business or enterprise context. (High proficiency)
  • Experience working with cross-functional business and technical teams. (High proficiency)
  • Knowledge of application delivery lifecycles, governance processes, and technology implementation practices. (High proficiency)
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and organizational skills. (High proficiency)
  • Ability to balance business objectives, risk considerations, and delivery timelines. (High proficiency)


Core Competencies

  • Demonstrated ability to interact in a positive, respectful manner and establish and maintain cooperative working relationships.
  • Ability to display excellent customer service to meet the needs and expectations of both internal and external customers.
  • Excellent listening and interpersonal communication skills to identify critical core competencies based on success factors and organizational environment.
  • Ability to effectively organize, prioritize, multi-task and manage time.
  • Demonstrated accuracy and productivity in a changing environment with constant interruptions.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze information, problems, issues, situations, and procedures to develop effective solutions.
  • Ability to exercise strict confidentiality in all matters.


Mobility

  • Primarily sedentary, able to sit for long periods of time.


Physical Requirements

Ability to travel within and around the facility or Work from Home (WFH) environment. Capable of using a telephone, computer keyboard, and mouse. Ability to lift up to 10 lbs.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Join Team CARFAX as a Senior Software Engineer

Isn't it time you bragged about where you work? At CARFAX, we do, every day. We pride ourselves on being mission-focused on helping to grow a brand built on accuracy and integrity. We care deeply about our products and our customers. We’re more than just a company: We help millions of consumers make more-informed decisions every day. We know that our teammates are our most valuable asset, and we value a balanced life while tackling challenging projects in a fast-paced environment.

At CARFAX, we build the data products that power automotive trust across North America. Our Data Technologies department owns some of the most critical internal systems at the company. This includes large-scale data enrichment pipelines, complex deterministic algorithms, internal data dashboards, vehicle data platforms, and a hybrid of cloud-native and on-prem infrastructure that ties it all together.

We are a team of engineers who care deeply about our craft. We build modern, well-tested software on real production systems that handle millions of records, and we have the autonomy to do it right the first time.

Our Development Culture:

Great software is built by great teams. A few things that make engineering in Data Technologies stand out:

  • Test-Driven Development (TDD): Quality is non-negotiable. We write tests first and hold each other to a high bar.
  • Pair Programming: We solve hard problems together and treat knowledge sharing as part of the job.
  • Autonomy: Teams decide how best to design, implement, and deploy their systems. Guidance and collaboration from other teams is plentiful, but development teams are trusted with the final call.
  • Agile Practices: We work in sprints, adapt quickly, and continuously look for ways to improve.
  • CI & CD: We leverage build and deployment pipelines to achieve consistent and repeatable artifact creation, testing, and deployment.
  • AI-Assisted Development: We use AI tooling across the engineering lifecycle including prototyping, test generation, code review, and documentation. We use it pragmatically and we own everything we ship.
  • Professional Development: We set aside dedicated time weekly for self-directed learning and tech exploration.

At CARFAX, we believe in the power of teamwork and value in-person interactions so that we can collaborate and thrive together. This position will require 2 days in the London, ON office per week, subject to change with future business needs.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Write Modern, Robust Code: You'll develop reliable, testable features across our full stack including Java-based backends, React/Angular and TypeScript frontends, and large-scale data pipelines.
  • Participate in Architecture and Design: You'll be involved in technology research, prototyping, and design decisions across cloud-native and distributed systems.
  • Employ TDD and Continuous Integration: Tests are not optional. Quality is enforced at every stage of the pipeline.
  • Lead and Mentor: You'll provide technical guidance, contribute to architectural decisions, and help grow the engineers around you.
  • Drive Platform Health: Security vulnerabilities, software currency, and tech debt don't fix themselves. You'll take ownership of keeping our systems healthy.
  • Leverage AI Tooling: We expect engineers to use AI-assisted tools like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or GitLab Duo as part of their day-to-day workflow. The expectation is that you have the fundamentals to know when to trust the output and when to throw it out.
  • Engage with Stakeholders: You'll work closely with Business Data Analysts, Product Owners, Leadership, and cross-functional teams to scope and deliver solutions.

What We're Looking For:

  • 5+ years of hands-on Object-Oriented Programming experience with a proven track record of delivering scalable, production-grade software solutions.
  • Strong JVM background with deep experience in Java or Kotlin and Spring Boot.
  • Modern frontend experience with React, or Angular, and TypeScript, building and shipping production single-page applications.
  • Proven experience designing, building, and maintaining robust, end-to-end data pipelines that support real-time and batch data processing at scale.
  • Solid experience developing and deploying applications in cloud environments, with a focus on scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency.
  • Strong hands-on experience with NoSQL and/or relational databases, with the ability to design efficient data models and optimize query performance at scale.
  • Strong proficiency with modern CI/CD pipelines (GitLab preferred), including branching strategies, automated builds, and continuous deployment workflows.
  • A genuine commitment to TDD, unit testing, and integration testing. Not just knowing what they are but actively doing them.
  • Proven capacity to lead, mentor, and guide engineering teams through complex technical challenges, driving best practices and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
  • A strong team player and clear communicator who thrives in collaborative environments, takes ownership of deliverables independently, and can articulate technical concepts, project requirements, and architectural decisions to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Additional Skills:

  • Proficiency with big data technologies such as Apache Spark and Hadoop, with experience processing and analyzing large-scale datasets in distributed computing environments.
  • Hands-on experience with core AWS services including Lambda, S3, SQS, and SNS, along with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform and AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK).
  • GraphQL experience, particularly with AWS AppSync or similar.
  • Kubernetes workload management or administration experience.
  • Exposure to multi-region cloud architectures and cross-account IAM.
  • Experience with MongoDB Atlas and MySQL.
  • A working understanding of how AI and ML systems consume data, including pipeline design for ML workloads, model input requirements, and how engineering teams support data science functions.
  • Demonstrated experience applying AI techniques and technologies to solve real-world business problems, including familiarity with natural language processing (NLP), computer vision, or other AI domains, along with experience integrating AI-powered capabilities into enterprise applications.

What’s in it for you:

  • Competitive Compensation: Attractive salary, comprehensive benefits, and generous time-off policies.
  • Retirement Support: 401(k) / DCPP matching.
  • Performance Rewards: Annual bonus program to recognize your contributions.
  • Innovative Workspace: Casual, dog-friendly offices designed for creativity and collaboration.

Hear from our Team: Our accolades speak for themselves:

  • 10X Virginia Business Best Places to Work
  • 9X Washingtonian Great Places to Work
  • 9X Washington Post Top Workplace
  • St. Louis Post-Dispatch Best Places to Work

Vacancy Status:
This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Base Salary:
The anticipated base salary range for this position is CAD $93,000 to $139,000 annually. Final base salary will be determined based on geographical location, experience, and qualifications.

Benefits:

Join a company that values your total wellbeing. Carfax offers competitive compensation, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and the chance to make a meaningful impact in an industry-leading organization. Our benefit offerings can be found at: CARFAX Careers.
