Vi forventer at afholde 1. og 2. ansættelsessamtaler i uge 49 og 50. 1. samtale vil være af normal karakter og 2. samtale vil tage udgangspunkt i et hændelsesforløb, hvor vi vil vurdere dine evner til at agere under en krise.

Om Klima-, Miljø- og Teknikforvaltningen
Klima-, Miljø- og Teknikforvaltningen varetager myndighedsopgaver og servicerer borgere og erhvervsliv blandt andet inden for miljøområdet, lokalplanlægning, byfornyelse, byggesagsbehandling og trafikområdet. Desuden er det Klima-, Miljø- og Teknikforvaltningen, der står for renholdelse, vedligeholdelse og udvikling af byens veje og parker samt foretager parkeringskontrol. Vi beskæftiger ca. 2.700 medarbejdere og administrerer et bruttobudget på knap 4,8 mia. kr.

title: Pædagogisk-psykologisk stedfortræder til Børne- og Ungeudvalget i Varde Kommune
description:
Vil du være med til at gøre en forskel for udsatte børn og unge? Familieretshuset søger pædagogisk-psykologisk stedfortræder, som indgår i Varde Kommunes Børne- og Ungeudvalg. Udvalget træffer afgørelse om blandt andet anbringelser og samvær for udsatte børn og unge, der er anbragt udenfor hjemmet.

Din viden er vigtig
Du vil blive udpeget som pædagogisk-psykologisk stedfortræder i Varde Kommunes Børne- og Ungeudvalg. Der findes et Børne- og Ungeudvalg i hver af Danmarks 98 kommuner. Udvalget består af to folkevalgte lokale politikere, en dommer samt to pædagogisk-psykologisk sagkyndige, hvor sidstnævnte udpeges af Familieretshuset.

Det er Børne- og Ungeudvalget, der træffer afgørelse, når en kommune ønsker at anbringe et barn eller en ung uden for hjemmet eller fastsætte rammerne for samvær. På baggrund af det samlede materiale, som kommunen fremlægger - herunder undersøgelser - skal du med din faglighed forholde dig til det udsatte barns eller unges situation.

Om dig
Der stilles ikke krav om, at du skal have én bestemt uddannelse, men du skal have en relevant psykologisk, socialfaglig eller en børnefaglig uddannelse. Derudover skal du have dokumenteret erfaring fra arbejde med udsatte børn og unge. Du kan for eksempel være uddannet psykolog, psykiater eller socialrådgiver med mangeårig erfaring og efter- og videreuddannelse inden for området.

Du skal kunne dokumentere:

  • Relevant videregående uddannelse
  • Relevant efter- og videreuddannelse eller kurser
  • Erfaring fra børne- og ungeområdet, herunder særligt udsatte børn og unge

Du skal således med din erfaring og vurdering kunne sikre, at afgørelserne hviler på et solidt børnefagligt grundlag, og i fornødent omfang tager hensyn til barnets bedste - i overensstemmelse med formålet med at yde særlig støtte til børn og unge. Derfor er det ikke afgørende, hvilken uddannelse du har, så længe du bringer din erfaring og faglighed i spil i komplekse og ofte svære beslutninger.

Arbejdets omfang og det praktiske
Det er Familieretshuset, der udpeger de pædagogisk-psykologisk sagkyndige til alle kommuner, mens kommunen står for udvalgsbetjeningen og godkender honoraranmodningen m.v.

Udpegningen gælder frem til og med 2029.

Det er svært at vurdere hvor mange gange du vil blive indkaldt. De fleste har hvervet som bibeskæftigelse.

Sidste år blev 95 % af sagerne afviklet på planlagte møder, men der kan opstå behov for møder med kort varsel - de akutte møder - inden for en uge. Det skal du derfor være indstillet på.

Hvis du udpeges, skal du oprette et CVR-nummer, hvilket er gratis for personligt ejede virksomheder. Du skal også være indforstået med både digital afregning og kommunernes digitale sagsbehandling.

Hvis du arbejder med børn eller unge i en kommune, kan du ikke være pædagogisk-psykologisk sagkyndig samme sted.

Honorar
Honorar afregnes på baggrund af en timetakst på 819,27 kr. i 2025, og så er der fastlagt et antal timer pr. sagstype. Se hele modellen for honorar i faktaboksen nederst.

Yderligere oplysninger
Udpegningerne sker i henhold til § 19, stk. 1, nr. 3, i lov om retssikkerhed og administration på det sociale område, lovbekendtgørelse nr. 354 af 2. april 2025. Grundlaget for udvalgets arbejde, herunder regler om medlemmernes habilitet til at deltage i afgørelsen af de enkelte sager, fremgår af forretningsorden for børne- og ungeudvalgene, bekendtgørelse nr. 1249 af 29/10/2025.

På hjemmesiden Kommunernes Børne- og ungeudvalg finder du henholdsvist:

  • Hvilke ansvar og vilkår der er gældende for hvervet, beskrevet i `Ansvar og vilkår´
  • Samt en beskrivelse af hvordan du beregner dit honorar under `Honorering´

Kontakt
Har du spørgsmål til udpegningen, er du velkommen til at sende en mail til: FRHBU@familieretshuset.dk. Vi vender tilbage til dig hurtigst muligt.

Ansøgningsfristen er søndag den 29. november 2026.
Der vil løbende blive indkaldt til samtaler. Samtalerne gennemføres på Teams.

Sådan søger du
Når du søger, skal du have dokumentation for uddannelse, efter- og videreuddannelse og erfaring klar.

title: Programme Officer (Protection Mainstreaming) (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Senior Programme Support Officer, USRAP, and the direct supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator, Protection Mainstreaming, and in close coordination with Movement Operations and Resettlement Support Center (RSC) Protection Mainstreaming colleagues and other relevant colleagues at the HQ level, the Programme Officer (Protection Mainstreaming) will support the USRAP by providing technical support and recommendations on a range of protection mainstreaming topics. In this capacity, they will have the following duties and responsibilities:

  1. Support IOM’s protection mainstreaming activities in the USRAP in the following broad areas: improving assistance to beneficiaries; analyzing risks, identifying protection gaps, and addressing those challenges by developing or supporting the development of guidance, tools, and training; monitoring and evaluating program and training activities for effectiveness in the context of protection mainstreaming; building networks and supporting dialogue; and providing training.
  2. Support centering the voices of beneficiaries and prioritizing their input and collaboration at all stages of USRAP work by:
    a. Working closely with the Senior Programme Coordinator to establish regular consultations with a wide variety of stakeholders, organizations, and forums in order to share updates on our work and solicit input and feedback.
    b. Helping to support the development of standards for receiving and incorporating stakeholder input, sharing outcomes, and responding to feedback, and reviewing existing Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) regularly to ensure they are accessible to all populations.
    c. When required, engaging in feedback sessions with populations to ensure their experiences are heard and considered in the improvement of USRAP activities.
    d. Supporting the RSC Protection Mainstreaming and Movement Operations teams in their direct work with beneficiaries and expedite programs.
  3. Work closely with colleagues in IOM offices hosting USRAP activities to develop and carry out risk analysis exercises. These exercises should determine where gaps exist in protection in the context of operational activities across the USRAP, and how those gaps can best be addressed.
  4. Contribute to the development of a wide range of guidance, tools, and training materials that are specifically tailored for IOM personnel working on the USRAP through research, reviewing, editing, and writing. Utilizing desk reviews of IOM materials, published research and guidance, and trainings from other organizations, site visits, discussions with personnel and managers, feedback from beneficiaries, and liaison with external organizations, gather the information needed to draft high-quality materials in line with established IOM and global standards.
  5. Along with the Senior Programme Coordinator, work with the relevant team in USRAP Global Coordination Office to develop and update monitoring and evaluation methodologies, approaches, and tools that will measure the effectiveness of protection mainstreaming activities and trainings and inform programming to enable further strengthening and continuous improvements. As needed, participate in monitoring and evaluation field visits.
  6. In coordination with the Senior Programme Coordinator, help guide and train relevant global networks of champions who support protection mainstreaming work within USRAP projects. Help ensure those networks maintain an output of high quality, transformative work that contributes to the continual improvement of USRAP activities globally and that they are regularly engaging with one another to exchange feedback and ideas.
  7. Regularly provide webinars and in-person trainings within IOM, and, if requested, other organizations. When needed, support the planning and delivery of regular Training of Trainers sessions and advanced training skills courses in person or by webinar.
  8. In relation to the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) and in close coordination with the Global Office and IOM HQ, serve as the PSEA Focal Point for the Global Office in Washington DC and all other IOM offices in the United States. Support day-to-day management of PSEA activities in the United States, provide technical input on PSEA activities, actively participate in the in-country interagency PSEA network and other coordination initiatives, and support implementation of the PSEA workplan and assigned actions.
  9. Serve as a resource for staff seeking advice on issues related to PSEA and follow established reporting requirements. Provide regular, effective PSEA training to all staff in the United States. Report as needed on PSEA work to the Global Office and IOM HQ.
  10. Contribute technical expertise on protection mainstreaming on behalf of IOM in a variety of internal and external forums, including UN system-wide initiatives. Participate in meetings, workshops, and international conferences on protection mainstreaming topics, as requested. As needed, write reports, presentations, and background documents on behalf of the USRAP and IOM. When possible, amplify the work of the USRAP across IOM, the UN system, and within resettlement and humanitarian contexts.
  11. Uphold Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards while carrying out all duties and responsibilities and demonstrate the ability to remain professional, impartial and unbiased during all interactions with migrants and colleagues per the IOM Standards of Conduct and instruction on the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). Alert the supervisor or management of any non-compliance to SOPs, Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards or IOM Standards of Conduct by IOM personnel or partners.
  12. Undertake duty travel, as required, to support monitoring missions, evaluations, stakeholder consultations, and capacity‑building activities.
  13. Perform any such other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Social Science, International Relations, Regional Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • Bachelor’s degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Experience working on protection mainstreaming issues in relation to programming in resettlement and complementary pathways, migration, United Nations, or international organization contexts is essential;
  • Experience developing guidance and training, and experience giving training, is required;
  • Experience in the USRAP, and particularly in activities requiring interaction with beneficiaries, is highly preferrable;
  • Experience speaking publicly on protection mainstreaming issues is an advantage.

Skills

  • Knowledge of current issues in the refugee context related to the protection of, and assistance to, a variety of populations is an advantage;
  • A demonstrated background and knowledge of issues related to migration, preferably in the international context, is essential;
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Stabilizing At-Risk Communities and Enhancing Migration Management to Enable Smooth Transitions (START) is an advantage;
  • Excellent computer skills and a high level of proficiency in spreadsheet and database applications;
  • Demonstrated knowledge of protection mainstreaming principles, including safety, dignity, accessibility, accountability, and beneficiary-centered approaches;
  • Proven analytical skills, including the ability to assess risks, identify protection gaps, and translate findings into practical recommendations;
  • Demonstrated training and facilitation skills, with the ability to deliver clear, practical, and engaging learning sessions to diverse audiences;
  • Excellent communication skills, including preparation of interim, final, and ad‑hoc situation reports;
  • Excellent organizational skills, including the ability to plan work, manage competing priorities, and meet deadlines;
  • Ability to consolidate and analyze information from multiple sources and produce high‑quality reports for donors, partners, and internal stakeholders;
  • Demonstrated interpersonal and coordination skills, including engagement with UN agencies, government counterparts, and implementing partners;
  • High degree of judgment, initiative, and ability to work independently within assigned areas.

Languages

IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish. All staff members are required to be fluent in one of the three languages.

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.


Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.


Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.


Notes

title: Teamleder til udrulning af Signalprogrammet
description:
Vil du være med til at sikre udvikling og fremdrift i en dynamisk 24/7/365 drift? Så har vi en spændende lederstilling, hvor du kan være med til at gøre en forskel for medarbejdere og vores trafikale leverancer.

Trafikstyringen af jernbanen, er med udrulningen af et nyt signalsystem, under forandring. Banedanmark søger en struktureret og engageret teamleder, der skal arbejde med at sikre at vi kommer i mål med de sidste udrulninger, får realiseret de forventede gevinster, implementerer nye funktioner og tilpasser vores arbejdsprocesser til organisationen.

Du vil indgå i en samlet ledergruppe bestående af i alt tre teamledere, hvoraf to refererer til en sektionschef. Du vil referere direkte til områdechefen.

Dit tjenestested vil for denne stilling være i Trafiktårn Øst i København eller Trafiktårn Vest i Fredericia, alt efter hvor du bor. Du skal forvente at have opgaver i begge trafiktårne og vil derfor rejse mellem de to lokationer efter behov.

Det overordnede ansvar som teamleder

Du skal være med til at sikre optimale rammer for medarbejderne i en travl og uforudsigelig hverdag, hvor signalsystemet implementeres i hele landet.

Dette sker blandt andet gennem udvikling og uddannelse af nye brugere til varetagelse af forskellige opgaver i det nye signalsystem, og gennem arbejdet med den konkrete udrulning på de enkelte strækninger.

  • Ansvar for alle SP-udrulninger på Trafiks vegne
  • Etablering af resterende funktioner i Trafikstyring
  • Sikre kvaliteten af TMS systemleverancerne og forberede overlevering til drift
  • Gevinstrealisering af Business Changes i Trafik
  • Tilpasse arbejdsprocesser
  • Være med til at sikre at leverancen fra leverandørerne lever op til kontrakterne.

Drifts- og personaleledelse

Som teamleder får du personaleansvaret for eget team, bestående af 4-6 medarbejdere. Teamet kommer til at bestå af specialister, eksempelvis superbrugere og udviklere. Under udrulninger af nye strækninger, indgår du i et samarbejde med ledere og medarbejdere fra de sektioner, der skal overtage de nye strækninger.

Ibrugtagningen af det nye signalsystem, fokuserer på forandringsparathed hos medarbejderne. Det er vigtigt for dig at engagere dig i kulturelle transformationer og styringen af forandringsprocesser, samt at tage initiativ til ændringer inden for personaleledelse og faglige områder.

Du får ansvaret for kompetenceudvikling og uddannelse af dit team. Du får til opgave at afholde personalerelaterede samtaler, herunder MUS, og du varetager den løbende kompetencestyring gennem coaching og motiverende samtaler i hverdagen.

Du kommer til at arbejde tæt sammen med de øvrige sektionschefer og teamledere i Trafikdivisionen, og du vil få en bred kontaktflade til specialister og teknikere internt i Trafik og på tværs af divisionerne i Banedanmark. Du vil her skulle kommunikere på flere niveauer i organisationen, og dele af denne kommunikation vil foregå på engelsk.

Leder af både personale og system i en forandringsproces

Vi lægger vægt på, at du som person er medmenneskelig, kan prioritere opgaver og sætte retning med flere forskellige opgaver samtidig. Du skaber rammerne for høj motivation og stor arbejdsglæde blandt dine medarbejdere. Du er åben for nye initiativer og går metodisk til problemstillinger og undersøger sagen til bunds, hvad enten det er et konkret problem eller en mere kompleks problemstilling. Du er engageret som person og sikrer, at opgaverne bliver løst, implementeret og fulgt op på. Du tager om nødvendigt de svære samtaler, og takler eventuelle konflikter, hvis de skulle opstå.

Det er ikke essentielt, hvilken uddannelse du har med i bagagen. Vi forventer, at du som personaleleder er fortrolig med at lede et team gennem god og synlig ledelse. Du er i stand til at bevare overblikket og kan effektivt navigere gennem omstillinger og forandringer.

Udviklingsopgaven er stor, - i forhold til systemudvikling og i forhold til at udvikle teams og mennesker. Her forventer vi, at du kan engagere dig og gøre en forskel.

Erfaring med processer for trafikafvikling og disponering ses som positivt.

Hvis du har en sikkerhedsfaglig baggrund og vil indgå i trafikstyringen, kan du som teamleder i Udrulning af Signalprogrammet, udføre sikkerhedsklassificeret arbejde, og du skal derfor opfylde helbredskravene på Trafikstyring jernbaneområdet. Det betyder, at du skal opfylde visse helbredskrav, og der bl.a. vil blive lavet en lægelig vurdering af hørelse, synssans, farvesans, sukkersyge, epilepsi, hjertekarsygdomme mv. Hvis du vil vide mere om kravene, kan du læse mere på Trafikstyrelsens hjemmeside (www.trafikstyrelsen.dk).

Løn

Du ansættes efter den til enhver tid gældende Fællesoverenskomst mellem Finansministeriet og Offentligt Ansattes Organisationer – Det Statslige Område (OAO-S-fællesoverenskomsten) og organisationsaftale for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og it-medarbejdere.

Stillingen er som udgangspunkt indplaceret i løngruppe 4 jf. gældende overenskomst, som du finder her og Medarbejder- og Kompetencestyrelsens lønoversigt, som du finder her.

Afhængigt af dine kvalifikationer og kompetencer er der mulighed for forhandling af tillæg. Der vil til den samlede løn være tilknyttet en arbejdsgiverfinansieret pensionsordning på 16 %.

Hvis du er tjenestemand og internt ansat i Banedanmark, vil du efter en konkret vurdering kunne bevare din tjenestemandsansættelse. Stillingen er klassificeret i lønramme 35.

Ansøgning og kontakt

Vil du vide mere om stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte områdechef Rene Makholm Hestbæk på tlf.: 2630 0918.

Har du spørgsmål til løn og overenskomst, er du velkommen til at kontakte vores HR-konsulenter på mail banedanmarkpersonale@BANE.dk.

Send os gerne dit CV og en motiveret ansøgning hurtigst muligt, da vi løbende vurderer og indkalder til samtaler. Går du videre fra de indledende samtaler, vil der blive indhentet referencer fra tidligere arbejdsgiver. Du vil blive informeret inden, at der bliver indhentet en reference.

For at søge stillingen klikker du på linket ”Søg stilling” og følger instruktionerne.

Vi ser frem til at høre fra dig.

Forskellige perspektiver gør os stærkere. Derfor værdsætter Banedanmark mangfoldighed og opfordrer alle interesserede kandidater, uanset personlig baggrund, til at søge.

title: MAGENTO ARCHITECT
description:
Magento Architect


Summary

We are seeking a highly seasoned Magento Architect to lead the strategic design and implementation of enterprise-level eCommerce solutions. In this pivotal role, you will oversee the full lifecycle of Adobe Commerce platforms, ensuring they meet complex business requirements while delivering exceptional performance and scalability. This position is critical for driving digital transformation initiatives, optimizing system architecture, and guiding technical teams in building robust, future-proof online retail environments that align with organizational goals.

Responsibilities

  • Define and execute the technical roadmap for enterprise eCommerce platforms, ensuring alignment with business objectives and industry best practices.
  • Architect scalable, secure, and high-performance solutions using Adobe Commerce and Magento 2, addressing complex integration and customization needs.
  • Lead the development team in adopting Agile methodologies to accelerate delivery cycles while maintaining code quality and system stability.
  • Conduct thorough analysis and implementation of web performance optimization strategies to enhance user experience and site speed.
  • Ensure seamless cross-browser compatibility and responsive design across all digital touchpoints.
  • Drive the adoption of Adobe Commerce certifications and standards within the organization to maintain technical excellence.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business requirements into detailed technical specifications and solution designs.

Requirements

Requirements:
  • Possess a minimum of 12 years of overall professional experience in software development, with at least 5 years dedicated to architect-level roles.
  • Hold a valid Adobe Commerce or Magento Certification demonstrating deep expertise in the platform ecosystem.
  • Demonstrate extensive hands-on experience in developing enterprise eCommerce platforms using Adobe Commerce and Magento 2.
  • Show proven proficiency in Agile development practices and leading cross-functional teams.
  • Exhibit strong capabilities in web performance optimization techniques to ensure high-speed, reliable applications.
  • Have a track record of ensuring cross-browser compatibility and resolving complex technical challenges.
  • Display a comprehensive understanding of enterprise-grade eCommerce architecture and scalability requirements.

Compensation

  • Annual Salary: ₹40 lpa

title: Contract Closeout Specialist
description:
SABG is seeking a Contract Closeout Specialist to support SZK within the U.S. Space Force by managing the final closeout of assigned Government contracts. This position ensures contractual end items have been delivered, inspected, and accepted, and that all outstanding administrative, financial, and reporting actions are resolved before recommending contracts for closeout. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with Government contract administration, closeout documentation, compliance requirements, and coordination with contracting officers, program managers, finance personnel, and other stakeholders to ensure contracts are properly and efficiently closed in accordance with applicable regulations and procedures.

This position is contingent upon contract award.

Travel: N/A

JOB TITLE: Contract Closeout Specialist

CLEARANCE: Active TS, SCI Eligible
LOCATION: El Segundo, CA

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

  • Perform final closeout reviews of assigned Government contracts to verify that all contractual requirements and obligations have been satisfied
  • Confirm delivery, inspection, and acceptance of contractual end items and ensure supporting documentation is complete
  • Verify that all administrative, financial, property, deliverable, and reporting actions have been resolved before recommending contract closeout
  • Review contract files, modifications, invoices, payment records, deliverable documentation, and other supporting records for completeness and accuracy
  • Identify outstanding contractual actions, documentation gaps, discrepancies, and unresolved issues that could delay closeout
  • Coordinate with contracting officers, contract specialists, program managers, finance personnel, contractors, and other stakeholders to resolve open items
  • Track contract closeout status, outstanding requirements, milestones, and suspense dates to support timely completion
  • Prepare closeout documentation, checklists, status reports, and recommendations in accordance with applicable Government requirements and organizational procedures
  • Ensure contract records are properly organized, documented, and maintained in accordance with applicable records management and retention requirements
  • Apply relevant Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements, agency procedures, contract terms, and organizational policies to closeout activities
  • Communicate closeout risks, discrepancies, and recommended corrective actions to appropriate Government and program leadership
  • Maintain accurate tracking systems and provide regular updates on closeout progress, issues, and completion status
  • Support process improvements that increase the accuracy, consistency, and efficiency of contract closeout activities
  • Manage multiple assigned contracts and competing priorities while maintaining attention to detail and compliance with established procedures.

SUPERVISION: N/A

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum Education: BA/BS
  • Bachelor’s degree in business, contract management, finance, accounting, acquisition, or a related field
  • Three to ten years of relevant experience in Government contracting, contract administration, contract closeout, acquisition support, or a related field
  • Demonstrated expertise in performing final closeout reviews of assigned contracts, including verifying delivery, inspection, and acceptance of contractual end items and confirming that all administrative and reporting actions have been resolved before recommending closeout
  • Experience reviewing contract files and supporting documentation to verify that contractual requirements, deliverables, and obligations have been satisfied
  • Experience identifying, tracking, and resolving outstanding contract actions, documentation deficiencies, financial discrepancies, and other issues that may prevent contract closeout
  • Familiarity with applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requirements, Government contract administration procedures, and contract closeout practices
  • Experience coordinating with contracting officers, contract specialists, program managers, finance personnel, contractors, and other stakeholders to complete closeout actions
  • Ability to review contractual and financial documentation for accuracy, completeness, and compliance
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple contracts, track suspense dates, and meet established deadlines
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document findings, communicate outstanding requirements, and provide clear closeout recommendations
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and support mission requirements in a structured Government contracting environment.

COMPUTER SKILLS:

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook, and the ability to maintain accurate contract tracking records

  • Skills in operating a personal computer and standard office equipment

COMPETENCIES: To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

  • Problem Solving - Identifies and resolves problems promptly; gathers and analyzes information skillfully; develops alternative solutions; works well in group problem-solving situations; and uses reason even when dealing with emotional topics
  • Written Communication - Writes clearly and informatively; edits work for spelling and grammar; varies writing style to meet needs; presents numerical data effectively; and able to read and interpret written information
  • Diversity – Shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences, and promotes a harassment-free environment
  • Ethics - Treats people with respect; keeps commitments; Inspires the trust of others; works with integrity and ethically; and upholds organizational values
  • Planning/Organizing - Prioritize and plans work activities; uses time efficiently; plans for additional resources; sets goals and objectives; organizes or schedules other people and their tasks if needed; and develops realistic action plans
  • Professionalism - Tactfully approaches others; reacts well under pressure; treats others with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position; accepts responsibility for own actions; follows through on commitments

LANGUAGE SKILLS: Ability to read, analyze, and interpret governmental regulations. Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and the public.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS: Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

REASONING ABILITY: Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to question activities and issues in all functional areas and make sound business decisions based on that data.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, talk, and hear. The employee is regularly required to write and type on a computer. The employee is frequently required to walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; climb, or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Job duties are performed in a manufacturing/office environment utilizing standard office equipment such as a computer, photocopier, and telephone. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate.

If because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process please contact our Recruiting team at recruiting@sabg.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

title: Sundhedsplejersker til Sundhedsfagligt Team
description:
Vil du være med til at sikre, at vi ser hele barnet? Har du lyst til at bruge din sundhedsfaglighed på en ny måde, opdage sundhedsproblemer hos udsatte børn og unge, styrke det tværfaglige samarbejde og udvikle en ny indsats i Københavns Kommune?

Så er det måske dig, vi søger til Sundhedsfagligt Team i Socialforvaltningen.

Om indsatsen
Vi opbygger et Sundhedsfagligt Team, der skal styrke sundhedsperspektivet i arbejdet med børn og unge i kontakt med kommunens myndighedsområde. Sociale udfordringer kan dække over sundhedsmæssige problemstillinger, fx vedrørende syn, hørelse, motorik, søvn, ernæring eller psykisk trivsel.

Teamet dækker fem geografiske områder i DSI. Du bliver som udgangspunkt tilknyttet ét fast område og får base på Islands Brygge. Du arbejder tæt sammen med områdets børne- og ungerådgivere og bidrager med sundhedsfaglig viden i børnefaglige undersøgelser. Du bliver bindeled mellem sundheds- og socialområdet og får mulighed for at præge indsatsen fra start.

Dine opgaver
Din hverdag veksler mellem faglig sparring, vurdering af sundhedsoplysninger, møder og sundhedsscreeninger.

Opgaverne omfatter blandt andet at

  • være sundhedsfaglig sparringspartner for børne- og ungerådgivere i sager med bekymring for et barn
  • gennemgå og vurdere sundhedsoplysninger, fx sundhedsjournaler, relevante attester og underretninger og identificere forhold, der bør undersøges nærmere
  • gennemføre sundhedsscreeninger som led i børnefaglige undersøgelser med fokus på fysisk og psykisk sundhed, udvikling og funktionsevne
  • deltage i møder om barnet og bidrage med sundhedsfaglige perspektiver på barnets samlede situation
  • besøge barnet i hjemmet efter behov, når det er vanskeligt at få barnet til undersøgelse, eller når familiens situation gør det relevant
  • udarbejde sundhedsfaglige vurderinger og dokumentation til den børnefaglige undersøgelse
  • identificere behov for yderligere undersøgelser eller støtte og hjælpe barnet videre til relevante sundhedsfaglige tilbud
  • følge op på sundhedsmæssige problemstillinger, eventuelt sammen med Udkørende SundhedsTeam, der arbejder om aftenen
  • udvikle og afprøve screeningsredskaber og arbejdsgange sammen med teamet

Du skal kunne se sammenhænge, stille relevante spørgsmål og supplere rådgivernes socialfaglige perspektiv med din sundhedsfaglige ekspertise.

Hvem er du?
Vi søger dig, der er uddannet sundhedsplejerske og har lyst til at bringe din faglighed i spil i et tværfagligt samarbejde mellem sundhed og socialt arbejde.

Vi forestiller os, at du

  • har solid viden om børns sundhed, trivsel og udvikling og kan omsætte den til faglige vurderinger
  • har erfaring med børn og unge i forskellige aldre – gerne med familier i udsatte positioner
  • kan analysere sundhedsoplysninger og identificere relevante problemstillinger, også når oplysningerne er komplekse eller ufuldstændige
  • er nysgerrig og undersøgende og ser sammenhænge mellem barnets sundhed, udvikling og sociale situation
  • kan arbejde selvstændigt og planlægge og prioritere din arbejdsdag
  • kommunikerer tydeligt med kolleger med andre faglige baggrunde og skaber kontakt og tillid til børn, unge og familier – også i vanskelige situationer
  • trives med tværfaglige møder, udvikling og forandring og har mod på at afprøve metoder og give feedback

Erfaring med tværfagligt myndighedssamarbejde, sundhedsfaglige undersøgelser eller udsatte børn og unge er en fordel. Det vigtigste er, at du har lyst til at bruge din faglighed på nye måder og udvikle indsatsen.

Vær med til at forme noget nyt
Teamet er under opbygning, og du får mulighed for at præge den faglige retning og arbejdsformen. Sammen skal vi udvikle screeningsredskaber, skabe tydelige arbejdsgange mellem sundhedsplejersker og børne- og ungerådgivere, kvalificere sundhedsperspektivet i undersøgelserne og opbygge et stærkt fagligt fællesskab.

Vi tilbyder dig

  • en central rolle i opbygningen af et nyt udkørende sundhedsfagligt team
  • mulighed for at præge screeningsredskaber, metoder og arbejdsgange
  • en selvstændig og varieret hverdag med faglig sparring, møder og sundhedsscreeninger
  • tæt tværfagligt samarbejde med børne- og ungerådgivere, Udkørende SundhedsTeam og andre relevante fagprofessionelle
  • mulighed for at gøre en konkret forskel for børn og unge, hvis sundhedsbehov ellers kan blive overset
  • fast base på Islands Brygge og som udgangspunkt tilknytning til et fast geografisk område
  • faglig sparring og løbende udvikling, mens teamet etableres

Vil du være med?
Har du lyst til at stille vigtige spørgsmål, udfordre vante perspektiver og sikre, at sundhed bliver en naturlig del af vurderingen af barnets behov? Så glæder vi os til at høre fra dig.

Ansættelsesvilkår
Du bliver ansat i Det Udkørende SundhedsTeam i Socialforvaltningen, Københavns Kommune, med fast base på Islands Brygge. Arbejdet foregår i dagtimerne mandag til fredag, og stillingerne er på 37 timer om ugen.

Tiltrædelse er den 1. januar 2027 eller snarest derefter. Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår følger gældende overenskomst.

Vil du vide mere?

title: DSP-Council Bluffs
description:

Direct Support Professionals (DSPs) provide daily support to individuals with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities, helping them live independently, safely, and meaningfully in their communities. Key Responsibilities
  • Support individuals with daily living activities such as cooking, cleaning, laundry, and household routines
  • Assist with personal care, hygiene, and medication support according to training and care plans
  • Transport and accompany individuals to appointments, work, errands, and community activities
  • Encourage independence, social engagement, hobbies, and personal interests

  • Complete habilitation activities and required documentation accurately and on time
  • Follow all health, safety, behavioral, and individual support plans
Required Qualifications
  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver’s license and current auto insurance
  • Reliable vehicle for transportation during shifts
  • Ability to pass required background checks

Preferred Experience – Not Required
  • Direct Support Professional
  • Caregiver or direct care experience
  • Intellectual or developmental disabilities
  • Healthcare or behavioral health
  • Human services or social services
  • Mental health support
What We Offer
  • Paid training and ongoing coaching
  • Supportive leadership and team-oriented culture
  • Opportunities for advancement, including Lead DSP and leadership roles
  • Tuition reimbursement for leadership positions
  • Wellness and gym reimbursement programs
  • Access to earned wages through DailyPay

  • $200 paid on the first paycheck after completing the initial two-week training

Schedule and Location

Pay and Compensation

Apply directly through Indeed or via our company website listed below. Our hiring team reviews applications promptly and will contact qualified candidates.

About Us
The Community Supports Network supports adults with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities to learn, grow, and thrive as active members of their communities. We focus on person-centered support, strengths-based services, and meaningful outcomes for the people we support and our employees.

title: Chanel Curator, Photographs
description:
Job Title: Chanel Curator, Photographs

Salary: £42,000 per annum

Contract Type: 12 months FTC, full time

Role Purpose:

The post of Chanel Curator, Photographs, will be a key member of the Photographs team within the Curatorial department and will play a significant role in the development, care and presentation of the Gallery’s outstanding collection of photographic portraiture. We are looking for a highly self-motivated individual with sound knowledge of photographic portraiture who will collaborate widely across the organisation and with external stakeholders. They will work across displays and exhibitions, as well as acquisitions, commissions, public events and digital content.

Key Accountabilities:

  • Working with the Gallery’s extensive photographs collection, the postholder initiates and delivers displays and interpretation both onsite and as part of the Gallery’s programme of national and international tours and contributes to the development of exhibitions.
  • Collaborates with period curators on the presentation of photographs throughout the Gallery’s chronological and thematic narratives.
  • Identifies opportunities for acquisitions and new commissions, with guidance from the Senior Curator, Photographs, and in line with the Gallery’s strategic priorities.
  • Undertakes collection management and cataloguing, develops scholarship and expertise in the photographs collection and photographic portraiture, sharing knowledge through public engagement.
  • Develops interpretation, publications and digital content and participates in the Gallery’s public programmes and media engagement.
  • Contributes to the Gallery’s public engagement through tours, talks, events and other activities.
  • Supports fundraising, partnership and acquisition activity through research and curatorial expertise.
  • Works collaboratively across the Gallery to contribute to successful project delivery.
  • The postholder will be encouraged to develop a network of artists, gallerists, patrons, scholars and other specialists and to represent the Gallery at openings and other photography-related events.

The above list is indicative but not exhaustive. As such, in addition to the key accountabilities and responsibilities listed the post holder may be required to perform other duties commensurate with the scope and/or level of the role

To read the full job description, please follow the link: Chanel Curator, Photographs.

Key Experience, Skills and Criteria:

  • Outstanding knowledge of photography, particularly practices related to portraiture, and a demonstrated interest in British art, history and popular culture.
  • A postgraduate qualification in the humanities, or demonstrable equivalent experience and evidence of written work on or towards relevant publications.
  • Relevant experience within a museum or gallery environment, with experience in curating displays and interpreting art for public audiences.
  • Strong research, analytical and written communication skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and to convey key information clearly, accurately and succinctly.
  • Ability to apply professional judgement to support practical solutions and successful project delivery and can work flexibly and meticulously under pressure.
  • Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively with colleagues.
  • A strong commitment to equality and diversity with the ability to balance differing needs.

We offer a competitive benefits package, including:

  • Generous pension scheme
  • 29 days annual leave allowance, in addition to bank holidays
  • Interest free season ticket and bicycle loans
  • Rental deposit scheme
  • Employee assistance programme
  • Free entry to many UK museums, galleries and exhibitions
  • Staff discounts on purchases in online shop
  • Professional & personal development opportunities

First round interviews will take place on week commencing 07 December 2026.

Please indicate on the notes section of your application form, if you will be unable to make these dates.

title: Ernæringsværter søges til faste weekender og som tilkaldevikar i Ernæringsenhed på Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospital
description:
På Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg hospital har vi en klar vision: vi vil være Danmarks fyrtårn inden for ernæringsbehandling.

Er du studerende inden for ernæring og brænder du for at gøre en forskel for patienterne? Er du omsorgsfuld og ser værtskabet, som en vigtig del af måltidet? Brænder du for at drage den omsorg og støtte for patienter og samtidig bidrage som en vigtig del af ernæringsindsatsen og det samlede behandlingsforløb? Så er du måske en af Bispebjerg hospitals nye ernærings-værter?

Værtskabet og omsorgen omkring maden spiller en stor rolle, og det skal varetages af ernæ-ringsværter udgående fra ernæringsenheden, og skal implementeres i etaper på alle senge-afsnit i 2026. Det indebærer, at der skal ansættes weekendafløsere som ernæringsværter i nye stillinger, som skal støtte patienter med at vælge den rette mad så deres ernæringsbehov dækkes under indlæggelsen.

Du skal trives i og se en spændende udfordring i at lande i en organisation under stor foran-dring, hvor mange ting ikke er faldet på plads endnu. Du bliver en del af ernæringsenheden, og skal være med til at finde de bedste løsninger med vores kollegaer på de forskellige afde-linger. Vi er her for patienterne, og de er omdrejningspunktet for vores beslutninger, initiativer og arbejdsgange. Vi er ambitiøse og vi gør os altid umage.

Du vil få din daglige gang på de sengeafdelinger, som du er tilknyttet, og du skal være med til at etablere nye tværfaglige samarbejder og nye arbejdsgange med din kollegaer fra afdelin-gernes øvrige faggrupper. Du vil ligeledes skulle indgå i et tæt samarbejde med de kliniske diætister samt tæt samarbejde med køkkenet, for at videreformidle patienternes feedback og ønsker til maden.

Vi søger 10 kollegaer til faste weekender gennemsnit 5,5 timer ugentligt

Stillingen som Ernæringsvært:

  • At være vært for patienterne og skabe trygge rammer omkring måltiderne
  • At motivere og støtte patienten til at vælge den mad og drikke som de har lyst til, og bestille det med udgangspunkt i den enkelte patients ernæringsmæssige behov, som diætisterne har fastlagt
  • Overblikket over patientens daglige kostindtag og mulighed for sammen med diætister at age-re på patientens daglige indtag, for at sikre de opnår deres ernæringsmæssige behov
  • At udføre kostregistreringer
  • Anretning af maden og servering af snack
  • At samarbejde tæt med diætister og plejepersonale for at sikre den optimale ernæring til den enkelte patient.
  • Du skal have lyst til at være med i en spændende og nyskabende forandringsproces, hvor du får en unik mulighed for at være med til at forme stillingen

Om dig:

  • Brænder for værtskabet og ernæring
  • Besiddelse af et godt overblik da der er mange bolde i luften
  • Du er studerende inden for ernæringsområdet, gerne Professionsbachelor i sundhed og er-næring
  • Du besidder gode samarbejds- og formidlingsevner
  • Du bliver motiveret af at indgå i det tværfaglige samarbejde med diætister og plejepersonale samt måltidsværter med patienten i fokus
  • Du trives med at arbejde selvstændigt, og er god til at strukturere og prioritere din tid
  • Du har masser af gå-på-mod og godt humør
  • Er imødekommende og kan skabe gode relationer til patienter.
  • Stabil og fleksibel

Du vil som ernæringsvært få:

  • Grundig introduktion til dine arbejdsopgaver og arbejdsgange
  • Tilknyttet til faste afdelinger
  • Et godt fællesskab, hvor vi lægge vægt på høj faglighed og trivsel

Vi tilbyder:

  • En spændende ny rolle, hvor du får mulighed for at være med til at forme funktionen som er-næringsvært
  • Tæt samarbejde med et tværfagligt team af diætister og plejepersonale
  • Et meningsfuldt arbejde, hvor du gør en forskel for patienternes ernæring og velbefindende

Faste weekend vagter i tidsrummet 14.30-20.00 hver 2. weekend og tilkaldevikarer med mu-lighed for ekstravagter ved ferie og sygdom

Du vil få en centralt beliggende arbejdsplads på Bispebjerg Hospital. Vi er organiseret under FM-enheden, og du vil referere til Chef for ernæringsværter Tanja Krogsbæk

Løn efter gældende overenskomst ikke ledende personale på sundhedskartellets område 32.17.1. eller Overenskomst for husassistenter m.fl. - 34.01.1

Send din ansøgning og bliv en del af et nyt fyrtårn for ernæringsbehandling:

Ansøgningsfrist onsdag den 25. november. Samtalerne afholdes i uge 49. Ansættelsesstart 1. januar eller efter aftale.

Ved relevante spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte Chef for ernæringsvær-ter Tanja Krogsbæk, tlf. 29136466 i tidsrummet 7.30-12.00.

Har du kvalifikationerne og har stillingen vakt din interesse, ser vi frem til at modtage din an-søgning

Om os
Enheden for Facility Management, i daglig tale kaldt FM-enheden, består af 500 ansatte for-delt på fem servicesektioner, der alle leverer ydelser af den højeste kvalitet, således at de kliniske afdelinger på hospitalet har de bedste forudsætninger for at kunne udføre deres ar-bejde – alt sammen til gavn for patienterne. FM-enheden er nemlig ikke bare en serviceorga-nisation; vi er en del af selve behandlingen.

title: Senior Programme Coordinator, USRAP Risk and Compliance (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

The United States Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP) operates globally, providing resettlement opportunities to refugees through a network of IOM-managed Resettlement Support Centers (RSCs), movement operations, migration health services, and associated program support functions. International Organization for Migration (IOM) Washington provides strategic oversight and direction for all USRAP operations, supporting global partners including the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration (PRM), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the Refugee Processing Center (RPC), and other stakeholders.

The Senior Programme Coordinator, USRAP Risk and Compliance, serves as the technical lead for risk management, internal controls, and program integrity across USRAP operations, ensuring that governance, regulatory compliance, fraud‑mitigation practices, and donor‑required controls are embedded throughout the program. The position integrates enterprise risk management, internal control reviews, compliance oversight, audit coordination, and fraud‑misconduct triage into a cohesive function that supports evidence‑based decision‑making and operational accountability for the USRAP.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Global and Domestic Programmes Unit, and the direct supervision of the Global Programme Coordinator, USRAP, the Senior Programme Coordinator, USRAP Risk and Compliance, has the following responsibilities and duties:

  1. Maintain and oversee the USRAP Program Risk Register, ensuring regular updates and facilitating periodic risk reviews with the Global Programme Coordinator, USRAP, the Deputy Global Programme Coordinator, USRAP (Movement Operations, Travel Loan Program (TLP), RSC), regional/hub focal points, and relevant Washington-based units. Ensure risk data is accurately reflected in the Organization’s risk‑management system for all USRAP projects.
  2. Plan, lead, and document internal control reviews covering Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) adherence, segregation of duties, workflow and system controls, data protection, and process integrity across USRAP operations. Issue written reports outlining prioritized recommendations, responsible parties, and timelines.
  3. Periodically review and approve Travel Loan Contact Center scripts and communication protocols to ensure full compliance with IOM policies, USRAP requirements, and applicable U.S. federal regulations—including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) and Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA). Verify that all beneficiary interactions are consistent, lawful, safe, and rights‑respecting.
  4. Monitor ongoing compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements governing loan issuance, repayment communication, collection practices, credit reporting, and record‑keeping. Ensure USRAP procedures meet donor expectations as well as IOM financial, operational, and data‑protection standards.
  5. Coordinate USRAP responses to internal and external audits—including PRM monitoring, Office of Internal Oversight (OIO) reviews, IOM internal oversight, and donor‑driven spot checks—in close collaboration with the Regional Risk & Compliance Officer to ensure institutional alignment. Track implementation and closure of all recommendations and maintain an audit‑ready evidence trail for all relevant processes.
  6. Monitor fraud‑risk indicators and red flags across USRAP operations, advise management on preventive and detective controls, and coordinate with the OIO, Ethics and Conduct Office (ECO), Legal Department, and other relevant units on follow‑up actions.
  7. Serve as the operational point of contact for USRAP fraud and misconduct reporting, ensuring timely triage, documentation, and routing of allegations in accordance with the USRAP Fraud & Misconduct SOPs and IOM’s global reporting mechanisms. Ensure safe, confidential, and accessible channels for reporting.
  8. Advise on the design and integration of internal controls for new processes, surge operations, system changes, and structural adjustments, in coordination with the Oversight Officer (Resettlement and Movement Management RMM)), Senior Health Operations & Compliance Officer (Migration Health Division (MHD)), Information Systems Owner, and other technical counterparts. Ensure necessary requirements are embedded in SOPs, workflows, and guidance issued to RSCs and operational units.
  9. Support management in developing, tracking, and validating corrective‑action plans, ensuring that remediation addresses root causes and is aligned with Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) findings, audit observations, and operational lessons learned.
  10. Provide guidance, capacity‑building, and training as needed to RSCs, Washington-based units, and field teams on risk management, internal controls, fraud prevention, compliance standards, and related IOM and USRAP policies.
  11. Safeguard confidentiality and ensure the integrity of all USRAP information by applying IOM data‑protection rules, USRAP confidentiality requirements, and applicable regulatory controls. As required, support global efforts to prevent and mitigate fraud across RSC and resettlement operations.
  12. Represent IOM/USRAP in technical meetings, working groups, workshops, and inter‑agency forums, as delegated.
  13. Uphold RMM Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards while carrying out all duties and responsibilities and demonstrate the ability to remain professional, impartial and unbiased during all interactions with migrants and colleagues per the IOM Standards of Conduct and instruction on the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). Alert the supervisor or management of any non-compliance to SOPs, RMM Protection Mainstreaming Minimum Standards or IOM Standards of Conduct by IOM personnel or partners.
  14. Undertake duty travel, including to high‑risk or complex operating environments, to conduct internal control reviews, support investigations, verify implementation of corrective actions, and provide onsite advisory support.
  15. Perform any such other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Risk Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Law, International Affairs, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
  • University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Minimum five years (seven with a University degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in risk management, internal controls, compliance, audit, or assurance functions, preferably within international organizations, multilateral institutions, or large operational programmes such as the United States Refugee Admissions Program (USRAP);
  • Demonstrated experience in designing, assessing, and strengthening internal control frameworks, including reviewing standard operating procedures (SOPs), segregation of duties, and operational processes relevant to refugee processing, resettlement support activities, and associated programme operations;
  • Experience identifying and assessing fraud and misconduct risks and advising on preventive and detective control measures in operational programmes, including the management of reporting channels and escalation processes;
  • Experience supporting the development and maintenance of programme risk registers, conducting risk assessments, and facilitating risk review processes with senior management and operational teams across multiple locations within large-scale resettlement or migration programmes;
  • Experience working in multi-stakeholder environments, coordinating with operational units, oversight bodies, and senior management to strengthen programme accountability, compliance, and internal control culture;
  • Experience developing and delivering guidance and training to operational teams on internal controls, risk management, fraud prevention, and compliance requirements in complex resettlement operations.

Skills

  • Familiarity with donor compliance frameworks and programme oversight requirements within large-scale migration or resettlement programmes, including adherence to institutional policies, regulatory obligations, and operational standards relevant to USRAP implementation, with awareness of applicable U.S. federal and state regulations, including financial and lending practices where relevant;
  • Proven track record in coordinating internal and external audit processes, including preparation of documentation, engagement with auditors, and tracking and implementation of audit recommendations and corrective action plans;
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze complex operational and programmatic information and translate technical inputs into clear strategic and operational guidance;
  • Proven capacity to coordinate across multiple units and technical pillars, facilitating effective communication and collaboration among diverse stakeholders;
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs within tight deadlines in complex operational environments.;
  • Demonstrated organizational judgment and problem-solving capacity, with ability to identify issues, assess implications, and support practical solutions;
  • Ability to provide guidance and direction to teams and colleagues in a dynamic and politically sensitive operational context.

Languages

IOM’s official languages are English, French, and Spanish. All staff members are required to be fluent in one of the three languages.

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.


Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 3

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.


Notes

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

title: Senior Model Risk Analyst
company: Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston
description:
The Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston is a leading provider of wholesale funding for housing and community finance in New England serving more than 420 financial institutions across the region. The Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston is committed to making New England a better place to live and do business, and our employees are integral to our success. As a cooperative, we are owned by more than 420 banks, credit unions, insurance companies, and community development financial institutions that access tens of billions of dollars of our reliable, wholesale funding each year. Our funds are a vital resource that helps our members succeed, provide families with safe, decent affordable housing, and generate economic development that creates jobs in communities throughout our region.

Our highly skilled team of 220 is innovative, collaborative, and passionate about the work we do. We seek other professionals excited to share their knowledge, talent, and passion for our mission to join our team. We offer opportunities for career development, robust benefits, and a work-life balance.

Position Summary

The Senior Model Risk Analyst will play a critical role in implementing and enhancing the Bank’s Model Risk Management framework, policies, procedures, and governance practices. As part of the second line of defense, the Senior Analyst will provide independent review, effective challenge, and oversight of models, modeling processes, and designated calculations used across the Bank.

The Senior Model Risk Analyst will independently lead reviews of complex financial, risk management, treasury, interest rate, liquidity, credit, valuation, accounting, mortgage, stress testing, and forecasting models used throughout the Bank, and will support the Bank’s model risk management approach to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, as applicable. Responsibilities include assessing model conceptual soundness, assumptions, limitations, data, implementation, controls, documentation, performance, and compliance with regulatory expectations.

The Senior Model Risk Analyst will routinely interact with model owners, senior management, external validators, auditors, regulators, vendors, and peers across the Federal Home Loan Bank System. The position requires substantial technical expertise, independent judgment, and strong communication skills.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a deep understanding of quantitative analysis, financial modeling, model governance, and regulatory expectations related to model risk management.

In this role, you will help strengthen the Bank’s ability to identify, measure, monitor, and control model risk. You will partner with model owners and stakeholders while maintaining independence, support clear and actionable validation outcomes, and contribute to enhancements in model governance, validation planning, performance monitoring, issue remediation, and risk reporting.

This role will have a hybrid work schedule in our Boston office in accordance with the Bank’s Hybrid Work Program. More time will be expected in the office to support onboarding initially.

Anticipated Pay Range

The anticipated base pay range for this role is $97,750 - $149,500

This role is based in Boston with weekly in-office expectations. The base pay posted represents the annual base pay range or hourly wage range that we expect to offer for this job opportunity. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including relevant experience, required skills and other relevant factors. The range noted here is not indicative of all positions in the job grade within which this position falls.

All Bank full-time positions are eligible to participate in our annual incentive program and our robust total rewards offerings, in addition to the base pay.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Independently lead and execute model validations and targeted model risk reviews for complex models, modeling processes, vendor models, and designated calculations.

  • Design and execute quantitative analyses including benchmarking, sensitivity testing, scenario analysis, stress testing, attribution analysis, outcomes analysis, and back-testing.
  • Evaluate model documentation, governance processes, change management practices, data quality, implementation evidence, and ongoing monitoring results.
  • Develop and present comprehensive validation reports, conclusions, and findings to model owners, senior management, committees, auditors, and regulators.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert on model risk management policies, procedures, standards, regulatory guidance, and industry practices.
  • Support regulatory examinations and internal audit reviews related to model risk management activities.
  • Assist in developing enhancements to model governance practices, model inventory processes, validation methodologies, risk reporting, automation, evidence management, and performance monitoring.
  • Mentor junior analysts and provide technical guidance, peer review, and knowledge sharing within the Model Risk Management team.
  • Conduct research on emerging modeling techniques, financial markets, model risk management practices, artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, and regulatory developments.
  • Participate in cross-functional projects and committees involving model risk, quantitative analytics, technology, data governance, and enterprise risk management.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills

  • Strong knowledge of model risk management, model validation practices, and model governance frameworks.
  • Strong understanding of statistics, econometrics, quantitative finance, risk modeling, and predictive analytics.
  • Strong proficiency in programming or analytical tools such as Python, R, MATLAB, SAS, SQL, or similar tools used for data analysis, statistical analysis, model development, or independent validation.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear technical reports and present conclusions to senior management and governance committees.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and deadlines.
  • Knowledge of regulatory guidelines and industry standards for model risk management, including FHFA Advisory Bulletins 2013-07 and 2022-03, SR 11-7/OCC 2011-12, SR 26-2, or similar model risk regulatory guidance.
  • Experience interacting with auditors, regulators, senior management, model owners, and third-party validation providers.
  • Must be able to work both independently and as part of a team.

Education

  • Master's degree in finance, economics, mathematics, statistics, financial engineering, data science, or a related quantitative field; a bachelor's degree with significant relevant experience may be considered.
  • Ph.D. in a relevant discipline, CFA, FRM, or similar professional designation is a plus.

Experience

  • Generally, seven or more years' experience in model risk management, model validation, quantitative analytics, financial modeling, model development, or related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading model validations and producing formal validation reports.
  • Experience with financial institution models, including interest rate risk, asset/liability management, valuation, liquidity, mortgage, credit risk, accounting, forecasting, stress testing, or fair value models.

  • Experience with vendor platforms such as PolyPaths, Summit, Principia, Yield Book, Numerix, Bloomberg, Moody's, or similar systems is a plus.
  • Experience supporting regulatory examinations and internal audit reviews related to model risk management activities.

title: Kickstart din karriere som speditørelev hos Nagel Danmark A/S
description:
Lokation: Nagel Danmark A/S, Padborg

Er du nysgerrig, arbejdsom og klar til at lære en branche, hvor tempoet er højt, og ingen dage er helt ens? Så er det måske dig, vi leder efter!

Hvem er vi?

Nagel-Group er en af Europas førende virksomheder inden for fødevarelogistik med speciale i køle- og frysetransport. Vi sørger for, at fødevarer bliver transporteret sikkert og effektivt ud til butikker i hele Europa.
Det kræver grundig planlægning, godt samarbejde og et stærkt overblik og her spiller du en vigtig rolle!

Hvad kommer du til at lave?

Du bliver en del af vores transportafdeling, hvor vi arbejder med internationale transporter. Du får en grundig oplæring og gradvist mere ansvar samt indblik i planlægning, koordinering og optimering af transporterne.

I starten arbejder du med at instruere og følge op på vognmænd, løse administrative opgaver og registrere performance. Du følger også op på transporter og ventetider.

Når du er klar til næste skridt, får du mulighed for at planlægge og koordinere ture og skabe overblik over dagens transporter. Samtidig får du indblik i økonomien og omkostningerne bag transporterne.

Hvem er du?

  • Du har gennemført et adgangsgivende skoleforløb til uddannelsen som speditørelev, f.eks. EUX og HHX eller STX, HTX og HF suppleret med et 5 ugers EUD-forløb.
  • Du er nysgerrig, arbejdsom og har lyst til at lære.
  • Du trives i en varieret hverdag, hvor struktur, overblik og ansvar går hånd i hånd.
  • Du behersker dansk og engelsk, og det er et plus, hvis du også kan tysk.

Du behøver ikke kunne det hele fra starten. Det vigtigste er din lyst til at lære og udvikle dig!

Hvad kan du glæde dig til?

  • En spændende elevplads i en international virksomhed.
  • Du bliver en del af et stærkt team, hvor du gradvist får mere ansvar.
  • Vi tror på, at vores elever er fremtidens nøglemedarbejdere - derfor investerer vi i dig og din udvikling.
  • Du får løbende sparring og støtte gennem din elevtid, så du får mest muligt ud af din uddannelse hos os.

Sådan søger du
Lyder det som noget for dig? Så send din ansøgning og dit CV via linket.
Vi afholder samtaler løbene indtil rette kandidat er fundet.

Har du spørgsmål, er du velkommen til at kontakte HR konsulent Mirna Hermannsen på tlf. 74308963

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig!

You will translate customer and market insights into a compelling, multi-year vision, align senior stakeholders and cross functional teams around strategic priorities, and build capabilities and operating models needed to deliver measurable merchant and business impacts.

    • Address systemic challenges across teams and hold the organization accountable for customer and business outcomes.
  • Build and lead a high-performing product organization
    • Hire, develop, and retain exceptional product leaders and managers, strengthening strategic thinking, product judgment, and outcome ownership.
    • Elevate product management practices, organizational capabilities, and operating models across the business.
