title: Customer Manager
description:
Customer Manager, Services

Are you ready to embark on a journey to help a technology & engineering company in decarbonization conventional power in Thailand. We are looking for a business-driven Power market specialist who has a hunger for customer value creation.

We have started doing business in Thailand more than 30 years ago and since then supplied 11 boilers to the market and serving many others. Now it is time for Sumitomo SHI FW to bring over 100 hundred years of comprehensive experience in thermal power plants to the plant owners to manage these extraordinary assets for next 30 years assuring the best production and availability.

Who are we?

Sumitomo SHI FW, shortly SFW, is a world leader in combustion and steam generation technology. We have sold over 500 circulating fluidized bed steam generating units around the world; to utilities, independent power generators, municipalities and industrial clients. Our leadership position in CFB combustion results from our commitment to deliver superior designs providing high efficiency, fuel flexibility and low emissions. We pride ourselves in being able to cleanly and reliably convert the widest range of low-quality fuels, waste materials and waste heat into affordable sustainable power, heat, syngas and steam for our clients. We are over 1 000 people globally and serve customers all around the globe.

What we can offer you?

Firstly, you will get a very wide position with endless opportunity to bring value by means of deep competence in boiler and combustion technology with project execution excellence.

You will have solid mandate to develop together with our customers ways of cooperation using Sumitomo FW’s widening portfolio for power producers. This will not be a “position with view” but a position where you will create “the view” together with the Sumitomo Experts and support from stable 450 years old company.

You will have an opportunity to create and participate in a new future for a company that does understand the need and opportunity to renew itself along with the disruption that is ongoing in the energy industry worldwide.

The role – Customer Manager, Services

We are seeking a proactive and customer-oriented Customer Manager to take ownership of customer relations throughout the full life cycle of the plants. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in cross-functional collaboration, enjoys working closely with customers, and is committed to delivering value-added solutions that ensure long-term satisfaction and performance.

As Customer Manager, Services, you will drive the Service business growth by

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for designated customers, ensuring strong and consistent customer relationships across the plant’s lifecycle.
  • Lead and coordinate customer service activities across internal teams (tendering, project management, technical service) to ensure successful project execution and customer satisfaction.
  • Manage proposal creation in response to RFQs, including technical and commercial documentation (proposal letters, appendices, time schedules, cost calculations).
  • Organize and lead internal and external kick-off meetings for proposals and awarded projects.
  • Act as Project Manager for assigned customer accounts, plants, and selected service projects, ensuring seamless execution and delivery.
  • Ensure technical and commercial alignment between customer needs and internal execution, working closely with plant management, operators, and engineering teams.
  • Manage Service Agreements, ensuring contractual obligations are met, and coordinate with the project controller for financial performance tracking.
  • Coordinate post-delivery warranty activities in collaboration with project teams..
  • Contribute actively to service business development initiatives alongside business directors.

In this role you will report to “Director, Customer Care, Thailand” and be located in Bangkok, Thailand – with some amount of domestic and international travel.

To be successful in this role, we expect

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in customer service, technical project management, or energy/power plant industry roles.
  • Proven experience managing cross-functional teams and coordinating customer-facing projects.
  • Strong commercial and technical acumen, with ability to understand complex technical issues and propose practical solutions.
  • Experience from maintenance and service business, background from power plant engineering is a plus.
  • Familiarity with maintenance contracts, Service Agreements frameworks, and aftermarket project execution is an advantage.
  • Strong plus if You already have an understanding of the energy industry and its’ value chains and value generating mechanisms, as well how technologies add value to customers business in it. At least you have a great appetite and capability to learn this fast based on your earlier experience.
  • You are keen on building strong relationships both externally with customers & partners and internally with colleagues cross-functionally.
  • You enjoy multitasking & challenges and are a high achiever with positive, can-do mentality and integrity
  • You have sound judgement and the ability for independent evaluation and decision-making
  • Fluent in English and in Thai language(s)

How to apply

Does this sound like an exciting opportunity? If yes, we would love to hear from you!

title: Lagerkoordinator
description:
Har du erfaring med lagerstyring, koordinering og samarbejde på tværs af afdelinger? Trives du med ansvar, struktur og en central rolle i den daglige drift? Så er det måske dig, vi søger som vores nye Lagerkoordinator.

Hos Vestergaard REHA Biler søger vi en engageret Lagerkoordinator, som kan være bindeled mellem lager, værksted, salg og øvrige interne funktioner. Du får en vigtig rolle i at sikre effektive arbejdsgange, høj kvalitet og optimal service til både kolleger og kunder.

Du bliver en del af et stærkt team i en forretning med over 25 kolleger, hvor samarbejde, faglighed og godt kollegaskab er afgørende for vores succes.

Om stillingen

Som Lagerkoordinator får du ansvaret for den daglige koordinering af lagerets aktiviteter og bliver kontaktpunkt mellem lager, produktion/værksted og salg. Du skal sikre, at reservedele, varer og arbejdsprocesser understøtter en effektiv drift, samtidig med at du bidrager aktivt til den daglige lagerfunktion.

Stillingen kræver både overblik, struktur og evnen til at arbejde selvstændigt i en travl hverdag.

Dine primære opgaver

  • Pluk af varer til ordrer

  • Modtagelse af varer samt kontrol i henhold til gældende standarder
  • Modtagelse af biler
  • Ad hoc-opgaver, herunder oprydning og optælling på lager

Om dig

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • Har erfaring fra lager-, reservedels- eller logistikområdet
  • Har erfaring med koordinering og planlægning af daglige driftsopgaver
  • Arbejder struktureret og har et godt overblik
  • Trives med at være bindeled mellem flere afdelinger
  • Er serviceminded og samarbejdsorienteret
  • Kan arbejde selvstændigt og tage ansvar for egne opgaver

  • Har kendskab til bilbranchen eller reservedele, hvilket vil være en fordel
  • Har gyldigt B-kørekort og truckcertifikat
  • Har fokus på kvalitet og detaljer

Vi tilbyder

  • En alsidig og ansvarsfuld stilling i en af Danmarks største bilkoncerner
  • Mulighed for at præge og udvikle arbejdsprocesser
  • En hverdag med tæt samarbejde på tværs af organisationen
  • Overenskomst inkl. pension og sundhedsforsikring
  • Et stærkt fællesskab med gode kolleger og sociale arrangementer
  • En arbejdsplads med fokus på trivsel, udvikling og medarbejderengagement

title: Person with Disability Internship – Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion
description:
Program Background

PARTISIPA is Australia’s flagship sub-national governance and resilience program in Timor-Leste. It works primarily with the Ministry of State Administration, the Ministry of Public Works, municipalities, and communities to strengthen national systems, improve municipal governance, and deliver sustainable and climate-resilient infrastructure. By combining support for policy reform, local government systems, and infrastructure services, PARTISIPA helps Government of Timor-Leste (GoTL) to deliver real benefits for citizens — more effective institutions, stronger community voice, and better access to quality services.

PARTISIPA support is delivered through three mutually reinforcing Pillars that together support a set of End-of-Investment Outcomes (EOIOs) that integrate infrastructure, governance, and resilience:

  • EOIO 1: National government better addresses the infrastructure and service needs of villages.

  • EOIO 2: Sub-national governments better deliver their mandated infrastructure and services.

  • EOIO 3: National and subnational governments have better systems and tools to provide sustainable and resilient subnational infrastructure to communities.

The three Pillars are as follows:

  1. National Systems to Support Municipalities: focuses on strengthening national policies, standards, and coordination among national level government stakeholders to ensure coherence, resilience, inclusion and clear mandates for municipalities.

  2. Municipal Governance Systems and Processes targets the functioning of municipal administrations through improved planning, budgeting, procurement, and participation, embedding citizen voice, GEDSI, and resilience into governance systems.

  3. Sustainable and Resilient Sub-National Infrastructure: integrates PNDS, rural water, and roads into a single framework for quality and sustainability, enhancing infrastructure coordination, embedding resilience and accessibility in design and operations and maintenance, using infrastructure as a governance entry point to build trust in municipal service delivery.

PARTISIPA mainstreams GEDSI across all components to ensure that government policies, planning and implementation processes continue to increase the visibility, voice, participation and agency of women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups.

About DT Global Asia Pacific

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see

The Role

  • To support PARTISIPA’s work on gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI).

  • To provide the opportunity for a person with disability to strengthen their career, skills and professional experience.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

Terms of Reference_Internship Persons with Disabilities.pdf

About You

Essential Experience and Knowledge

  • Has experience working or volunteering on projects or organisations that work in Disability inclusion, gender equality, community development, social work, public administration, infrastructure or other relevant areas.
  • Basic computer ability (e.g. MS Word, Excel, Power point and email)
  • Interest in disability inclusion, public administration, community development and infrastructure.
  • Interest to learn and build their professional opportunities in a work environment that is inclusive.
  • Strong ability to work in a team and with people of different cultures.
  • Strong ability to read and write in Tetun
  • Strong work ethic
  • Health and Safety Requirement: For roles requiring travel, particularly to rural or remotes areas, candidates must be willing to comply with program health and safety requirements, including participation in safety briefings, adherence to risk mitigation measures, and, where applicable, vaccination requirements (e.g. rabies).

Desirable

  • Diploma or relevant training or education in program management, gender equality, disability inclusion, social work, Communty development, international relations, public administration or equivalent.

  • An understanding about infrastructure accessibility

  • Ability to speak English

This position will be for 12 months. It is open only to persons with disabilities. Women with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Any accessibility needs will be accommodated and supported in the workplace by PARTISIPA.

Why join PARTISIPA?

By joining the PARTISIPA Program, you will be part of an environment where you can collaborate with leading experts from diverse backgrounds, access development programs to achieve your career goals, and be challenged to take a global outlook.

HOW TO APPLY
Click the 'Apply Now' button.

Please submit
1) Your CV
2) A cover letter addressing the selection criteria


APPLICATIONS CLOSE November 18, 2026 – 5pm Dili time (GMT+9)

Should this role be of interest, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Kindly note only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

People with lived experience of the regions in which DT Global operates are strongly encouraged to apply. DT Global welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including First Nations peoples, diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC), and people with disabilities.

We take a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harm of adults and children; fraud, corruption and bribery; modern slavery; and any form of exploitation across our operations, partnerships, and supply chains. title: Senior Partnerships Officer (P)
description:
Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

  1. Internal candidates
  2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu

Second tier candidates include:
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

Organizational Context and Scope

The IOM Global Office in Brussels acts as IOM’s liaison and coordination office to European Union institutions, bodies and agencies. It supports IOM’s strategic engagement with the European Union and other Brussels-based partners across policy dialogue, programme coordination, resource mobilization, partnership development, research, advocacy and external positioning.

The Office engages with a broad range of partners, including European Union institutions and agencies, Member States, United Nations agencies, international and regional organizations, financial institutions, the private sector, trade unions, academia, think tanks, non-governmental organizations and the media.

Under the overall strategic supervision of the Director of the IOM Global Office in Brussels, the direct supervision of the Policy and Programme Support Division (PPSD) Chief, and in coordination with relevant PPSD colleagues, the Senior Partnerships Officer will lead and coordinate IOM’s engagement with the European Union and Brussels-based partners, with a particular focus on Global Gateway and related Team Europe Initiatives in support of the European Union and IOM’s migration priorities.

The Senior Partnerships Officer will contribute to strategic policy analysis, programme coordination, resource mobilization, partnership strategy and development and strategic advisory functions to IOM offices worldwide on European Union-related partnerships related to Global Gateway. The role will support IOM’s positioning by identifying opportunities to connect migration governance, forced displacement, mobility, skills, climate action, resilience, digitalization, private sector engagement and sustainable investment.

They will work closely with Resource Mobilization, Programme Support, Private Sector Partnerships Divisions and relevant thematic teams to ensure coherent, strategic and results-oriented engagement with European Union institutions, Member States and other partners.

1. In coordination with the PPSD Chief, lead and strengthen IOM’s strategic engagement with European Union institutions, bodies and agencies, with a particular focus on Global Gateway and Team Europe initiatives related to the EU and IOM migration priorities.
2. Serve as a thematic focal point and strategic advisor on Global Gateway-related partnerships, identifying entry points for IOM engagement in areas such as mobility, forced displacement, skills, digitalization, climate action, infrastructure, trade facilitation, private sector engagement, resilience, and sustainable investment.
3. Ensure effective coordination between the IOM Global Office in Brussels, Resource Mobilization, Programme Support, Private Sector Partnerships Divisions at HQ, and relevant technical teams to support coherent and strategic engagement with European Union institutions, Member States and other partners on Global Gateway-related partnerships.
4. Contribute and represent IOM in policy dialogue and strategic positioning with Brussels-based stakeholders, including European Union institutions, Member States, United Nations agencies, international financial institutions, private sector actors, trade unions, think tanks, academia, civil society and the media.
5. Provide technical and strategic support to IOM country offices, regional offices and headquarters departments on European Union-related engagement related to the Global Gateway programming, Team Europe approaches, donor priorities, and partnership development.
6. In coordination with the Policy and Programme Support Division (PPSD) Chief and the RM Division, identify and develop partnership and resource mobilization opportunities linked to the European Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) as relevant to the European Union external action and Global Gateway investment priorities.
7. In coordination with the PPSD Chief and the PSP Division, identify and develop partnership and resource mobilization opportunities linked to the European Development private sector actors as relevant to the European Union external action and Global Gateway investment priorities.
8. Lead and coordinate the design and development of concept notes, proposals, briefing materials and partnership products, ensuring alignment with IOM priorities, European Union policy frameworks, donor requirements and partner expectations.
9. Facilitate internal coordination, capacity building and knowledge sharing on Global Gateway and European Union partnership opportunities, including through briefings, mapping exercises, internal guidance notes and strategic updates for IOM offices and field visits as required.
10. Monitor European Union policy, funding and partnership developments, particularly those relevant to Global Gateway, and provide strategic recommendations to senior management and relevant stakeholders.
11. Support IOM’s visibility and communications on European Union partnerships, including the preparation of talking points, donor updates, strategic messages, event inputs, success stories and external-facing materials.
12. Represent IOM, as required, in relevant meetings, consultations, events and coordination platforms with European Union institutions, Member States, international organizations, private sector actors and other Brussels-based partners.
13. Contribute to programme coordination and quality assurance for Brussels-based and European Union-funded initiatives, including through monitoring of implementation progress, support to reporting, risk identification and follow-up on operational or partnership issues.
14. Support research, analysis and advocacy efforts that strengthen IOM’s role as a strategic partner to the European Union, particularly in relation to Global Gateway, related mobility partnerships, sustainable investment, whole-of-route approaches and cooperation with countries of origin, transit and destination.
15. Undertake duty travel as required to support partnership development, programme coordination, donor engagement, monitoring and representation.
16. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Master’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law, Business, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or
  • University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.
  • Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Proven experience in European Union external action, international partnerships, resource mobilization, or programme coordination is required;
  • Experience engaging with European Union institutions, Member States, diplomatic missions, United Nations agencies, international organizations, civil society, academia, think tanks, media and/or private sector partners is required;
  • Progressively responsible experience in project or programme management, donor coordination, administration, or partnership development is required;
  • Demonstrated experience in donor liaison, proposal development, donor reporting, briefing materials, communications, and visibility activities is required;
  • Experience supporting multi-country, regional or global programmes, including coordination with country offices, regional offices or headquarters functions, is required;
  • Experience working on Global Gateway, Team Europe Initiatives, European Union funding instruments, external investment, sustainable development, mobility, climate, digitalization, skills, resilience or private sector engagement is highly desirable;
  • Experience managing or supporting international multi-stakeholder partnerships involving governments, international organizations, financial institutions, private sector actors and civil society is highly desirable; and,
  • Experience in organizational strategic planning, institutional positioning, knowledge management or change management is highly desirable.

Skills

  • Knowledge of European Union institutions, external action frameworks and funding instruments is required;
  • Knowledge of Global Gateway, Team Europe Initiatives, international partnerships and sustainable investment is highly desirable;
  • Knowledge of the United Nations system is required;
  • Understanding migration governance and its links with development, mobility, skills, climate, resilience and private sector engagement is desirable;
  • Excellent writing, communication, negotiation and representational skills;
  • Proven analytical skills and ability to draft and edit technical and strategic documents;
  • Excellent political judgement and ability to identify partnership and resource mobilization opportunities;
  • Demonstrated interpersonal skills and ability to maintain effective working relationships with diverse counterparts;
  • Capacity for strategic and creative thinking;
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team; and,
  • Proven organizational and time management skills, with ability to deliver under tight timelines.

Languages

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
  • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
  • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
  • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 3

  • Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
  • Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
  • Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
  • Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
  • Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 3

  • Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
  • Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
  • Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.
  • Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction.
  • Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings.

Notes

IInternationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to all clearances, including medical and security as well as accreditation, any residency or visa requirements. Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and any forms of discrimination. IOM is committed to promote the protection and safeguarding of all children.

IOM conducts reference checks and background verification, including through system wide databases such as ClearCheck, to help ensure that candidates have no record of misconduct, including on sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, or fraud. Candidates are expected to uphold these standards and principles at all times.

IOM does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process—whether for application, interview, processing, training, or otherwise—and does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM WAVE system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies
